MY.summary: Since about mid-2024 Malaysia has stopped approving new data centres that do not serve AI or high-technology use, according to the Prime Minister. Every new project now needs clearance from a federal Data Centre Task Force, and that clearance depends on spare power and water. Johor hosts most of the country's capacity and has paused new water-cooled builds until about mid-2027.

approvals.title: Non-AI data centres no longer approved
approvals.text: The Prime Minister told Parliament that new data centre applications with no link to AI or high technology have been stopped. He said the restriction had been in place for nearly two years. No formal end date was given.

sources.title: Non-AI Data Centres Restricted, Power And Water Supply Sufficient
Malaysia's data centre policy is saying the quiet part out loud

approvals.title: Federal task force clears every project
approvals.text: MIDA (Malaysian Investment Development Authority) is the lead agency for all new and expansion data centre applications. The Data Centre Task Force is co-chaired by the trade ministry MITI and the Ministry of Digital. It received more than 40 applications in 2026 and scores them on investment value, energy and water efficiency, connectivity and economic contribution.

sources.title: Malaysia to introduce Sustainable Data Centre Framework by October
Malaysia Data Centre Task Force Gets Over 40 Applications In 2026

approvals.title: Approval only with spare power and water
approvals.text: MITI said data centre projects will be approved only when energy and water supply is sufficient. Residents get first call on water.

sources.title: Government to approve data centre projects only if energy, water supply are sufficient, says Miti

approvals.title: Proof of demand needed before approval
approvals.text: New projects need task force approval and must show secured demand, such as offtake agreements, and proof of financial close. The rule aims to filter out speculative power requests.
approvals.authority: MITI, Energy Commission, Data Centre Task Force

sources.title: Issues: Data centres to comply with revised electricity supply plan

approvals.title: Johor approves only Tier 3 and 4
approvals.text: Johor stopped approving Tier 1 and Tier 2 data centres. These are lower-redundancy designs that the state says use far more water. New sites must sit in industrial zones and use reclaimed water instead of the public supply.

sources.title: No More Approvals For Tier 1 And Tier 2 Data Centres In Johor

approvals.title: Selangor requires utility sign-off
approvals.text: Selangor will not approve a data centre unless TNB confirms power supply and Air Selangor confirms water supply. Each project also needs clearance from the federal task force.

sources.title: No data centre approval without enough water, power, says Selangor MB

power.title: Highest tariff class for large sites
power.text: The RP4 tariff took effect on 1 July 2025. RP4 is the regulatory period that sets TNB's base tariff. Data centres above 100MW fall into the ultra-high voltage class, which pays the highest rates. Analysts put the cost at about 60 sen per kWh, 10 to 15 percent above the old tariff.

sources.title: Data centres in Malaysia to pay 10%-15% more for electricity, analysts say
Malaysia imposes power tariffs for data centers

power.title: Use it or pay a makeup charge
power.text: Data centre supply agreements require 85 percent use of declared maximum demand in the first four years and 75 percent in years 5 to 6. A shortfall is billed at RM8.50 per kW each month.

sources.title: Issues: Data centres to comply with revised electricity supply plan

power.title: TNB has 8.3GW contracted to data centres
power.text: TNB has signed electricity supply agreements for 59 data centre projects totalling 8.3GW. All are five-year take-or-pay contracts, so the customer pays even if it uses less. About 68 percent of the capacity is in Johor.

sources.title: TNB Locks In Growth Securing 59 Data Centre Projects With 8.3GW Capacity

power.title: Data centres use 9.28% of national power
power.text: The Energy Commission said data centres used 9.28 percent of national electricity, with about 0.8GW live and about 3GW in applications. It set no cap on data centre power and approves connections based on system capacity.

sources.title: Data centres account for 9.28% of total electricity consumption
Data centres and prolonged heat are pushing Malaysia's power demand higher

power.title: CRESS grid fee cut to 14 sen
power.text: CRESS (Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme) lets a large buyer take green power from a developer over TNB's grid for a system access charge. The charge for firm supply fell from 20 to 14 sen per kWh for projects running by 31 December 2028. Contracts must run at least 10 years.
power.authority: Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (PETRA)

sources.title: Solar gold rush gets CRESS lift
Reduced System Access Charge For CRESS Could Accelerate Solar, Battery Investments, Says MBSB

power.title: Onsite generation being tested at DayOne
power.text: DayOne signed an MoU (memorandum of understanding) with TNB Power Generation on 7 August 2026 to study up to 1.5GW of onsite power with battery storage at a Selangor campus. The fuel type was not disclosed. The plan still needs feasibility work and regulatory approval.

sources.title: DayOne and TNB Explore Up To 1.5 GW of On-Site Power Generation to Advance Malaysia Energy Resilience and Digital Economy

incentives.title: DESAC tax break for data centres
incentives.text: DESAC (Digital Ecosystem Acceleration Scheme) gives new data centre companies a 60 or 100 percent Investment Tax Allowance for 5 to 10 years. They can choose a 10 or 15 percent tax rate instead. Existing companies get 30 or 60 percent for 5 years, capped at 70 percent of income.

sources.title: Digital Ecosystem Acceleration (DESAC) Guideline
TaXavvy Issue 1-2025

incentives.title: DESAC requires local jobs and vendors
incentives.text: At least half of staff must be full-time Malaysians earning RM5,000 a month or more. Applicants also need two local vendor programmes and at least one green technology.

sources.title: Digital Ecosystem Acceleration (DESAC) Guideline

incentives.title: Green design targets tied to incentives
incentives.text: The Guideline for Sustainable Development of Data Centre sets design PUE targets of 1.4 to 1.7. PUE (power usage effectiveness) is total site power divided by IT power. The guideline also targets WUE of 2.2 cubic metres per MWh or lower, and meeting it is a condition for DESAC incentives.

sources.title: Guideline for Sustainable Development of Data Centre
TaXavvy Issue 1-2025

incentives.title: Data centres took 44% of approvals
incentives.text: MIDA approved RM95.8 billion of data centre investment in the first half of 2026. That was 44 percent of all approved investment. Cumulative data centre approvals since 2021 reached RM385.7 billion.

sources.title: Malaysia Data Centre Task Force Gets Over 40 Applications In 2026
Malaysia Secures RM218.5 Billion in Approved Investments In 1h 2026, With Domestic Investment in Manufacturing Up 23%

data.title: Transfer whitelist removed from PDPA
data.text: An amendment to the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) took effect on 1 April 2025. It replaced the government list of approved countries with a test. Personal data may go to countries with substantially similar protection.

sources.title: Save the Dates: Personal Data Protection Amendments Now in Operation

data.title: Cross-border transfer guideline issued
data.text: The PDP Commissioner's guideline accepts binding corporate rules, standard contract clauses and certification as transfer tools. Transfer impact assessments are valid for up to three years. The guideline sets no data localisation rule.

sources.title: Launch of Personal Data Protection Guideline for Cross Border Data Transfers

data.title: Breach notice and DPO duties live
data.text: From 1 June 2025, data controllers must appoint a data protection officer and report data breaches.

sources.title: Save the Dates: Personal Data Protection Amendments Now in Operation

data.title: Bank Negara tech risk rules revised
data.text: Bank Negara Malaysia revised its RMiT (Risk Management in Technology) policy, which governs how financial institutions manage technology and cyber risk. The revision took effect on 28 November 2025. It also adds Code of Practice duties for critical national infrastructure.

sources.title: Revised Policy Document on Risk Management in Technology (RMiT)
Bank Negara Malaysia revises policy document on Risk Management in Technology

data.title: Sovereign cloud for state data planned
data.text: The Prime Minister said Malaysia will build secure storage for sensitive government and citizen data. He cited concern over the US CLOUD Act. No rules have been published.

sources.title: Malaysia seeks sovereign cloud to safeguard national data
Single licensing authority to streamline Malaysia's booming data centre sector

water.title: Johor pauses water-cooled expansions
water.text: Johor told data centres that rely on water for cooling to wait at least 18 months for new supply, to about mid-2027. The state cites distribution limits during drought. MITI said in February 2026 that no investment had been deferred as a result.

sources.title: Data centres in Malaysia's Johor told to wait for water 'until mid-2027'
Malaysia sees no data centre delays despite Johor's water‑supply pause, says Miti

water.title: Johor data centre water tariff
water.text: A separate water tariff for data centres in Johor took effect on 1 August 2025. The rate is RM5.33 per cubic metre.

sources.title: Johor's water tariff adjustment: Data centres would have to pay more

water.title: Reclaimed water first for cooling
water.text: SPAN, the National Water Services Commission, issued guidelines on alternative water sources in September 2025. They ask data centres to cool with reclaimed water where available, or with air-cooled systems that discharge no water.

sources.title: Johor data centres turn to recycled water

water.title: Johor requires reclaimed water
water.text: New Johor data centres must use reclaimed water instead of drawing from Ranhill SAJ, the state water utility. Two reclaimed water plants serve data centres today, at Ulu Tiram and Gelang Patah. Both treat Indah Water effluent.

sources.title: No More Approvals For Tier 1 And Tier 2 Data Centres In Johor
Johor data centres turn to recycled water

water.title: WUE target and water stress siting
water.text: The national sustainable data centre guideline targets WUE of 2.2 cubic metres per MWh or lower, falling to 2.0 within 10 years. WUE (water usage effectiveness) measures water use per unit of IT energy. The guideline also steers sites in Peninsular Malaysia to areas with a water stress index below 0.8.

sources.title: Guideline for Sustainable Development of Data Centre

water.title: Johor technical committee vets water use
water.text: Johor set up a Special Technical Committee in August 2025 to vet every data centre project for its effect on water demand. It draws on state and federal technical agencies and is chaired by the state public works, transport, infrastructure and communication committee chairman. Johor applies a water usage effectiveness (WUE) threshold of 1.8, the same as Singapore.
water.authority: Johor State Government, Special Technical Committee

sources.title: Amid fears of water crisis by 2030, Johor govt sets up special committee to vet data centres' impact on demand

water.title: JSW and IWK supply reclaimed water in Johor
water.text: Johor Special Water (JSW), a state government company, and Indah Water Konsortium (IWK), the national sewerage operator, supply up to 12 million litres a day of treated effluent to data centres. The water runs from IWK's Taman Pelangi Indah plant through a 6.5 kilometre pipeline to Bridge Data Centres, Computility Technology and DayOne. JSW also has an agreement to supply DayOne with raw water from Sungai Tebrau.
water.authority: Johor Special Water (JSW), Indah Water Konsortium (IWK)

sources.title: IWK Supplies 12 MLD Reclaimed Water To Johor Data Centres

watching.title: Budget 2027 due early October
watching.text: The government said Budget 2027 would be tabled in early October 2026. Any change to data centre incentives would likely appear there.

sources.title: Budget 2027 to be tabled in early October, says PM Anwar

watching.title: National PUE, WUE and CUE standards
watching.text: The Energy Commission and SPAN are drafting standards for power, water and carbon efficiency. CUE (carbon usage effectiveness) measures emissions per unit of IT energy. No issue date has been announced.

sources.title: Malaysia Data Centre Task Force Gets Over 40 Applications In 2026

watching.title: Single data centre licensing authority
watching.text: MITI said in November 2025 that a single licensing authority for data centres would be set up. No law or start date has been published.

sources.title: Single licensing authority to streamline Malaysia's booming data centre sector

watching.title: Johor water pause ends about mid-2027
watching.text: Johor's hold on new water-cooled capacity is due to run to about mid-2027. Johor and the federal government are funding RM5 billion of new reservoirs and treatment plants.

watching.text: DESAC incentives and the sustainable data centre guideline apply to applications MIDA receives by 31 December 2027.

watching.text: Projects must reach commercial operation by 31 December 2028 to lock in the 14 sen CRESS access charge.

authorities.name: Data Centre Task Force (MITI and the Ministry of Digital)
authorities.role: Every new or expanded project needs its clearance. It scores applications on investment value, energy and water efficiency, connectivity and economic contribution. It approves only where spare power and water exist and the developer shows secured demand and financial close.

authorities.name: Prime Minister's Office
authorities.role: Sets the national line. The Prime Minister told Parliament in February 2026 that new data centres with no AI or high-technology link have been stopped. He has also promised a sovereign cloud for sensitive government and citizen data.

authorities.name: Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA)
authorities.role: The lead agency that receives every new and expansion application. It also grants the DESAC tax incentives, which require Malaysian jobs, local vendors and the green design targets. It approved RM95.8 billion of data centre investment in the first half of 2026.

authorities.name: Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB)
authorities.role: The national utility in Peninsular Malaysia. A project is real once TNB signs its electricity supply agreement, and TNB has signed 8.3GW across 59 projects on five-year take-or-pay terms. Selangor now needs TNB to confirm supply before it approves a site.

authorities.name: Energy Commission (Suruhanjaya Tenaga)
authorities.role: Regulates tariffs and grid connections. Large data centres pay the highest RP4 tariff class and a makeup charge if they use less power than declared. It approves connections on system capacity and is drafting national efficiency standards.

authorities.name: Johor State Government
authorities.role: Johor hosts most of the country's capacity and sets the strictest local terms. Its Special Technical Committee vets every project's water demand against a WUE threshold of 1.8. It approves only Tier 3 and Tier 4 designs in industrial zones, requires reclaimed water, and has paused new water-cooled capacity to about mid-2027.

authorities.name: Johor water suppliers (JSW, IWK and Ranhill SAJ)
authorities.role: Because Johor requires reclaimed water, these suppliers decide whether a new site can cool. Johor Special Water (JSW), a state company, and Indah Water Konsortium (IWK), the national sewerage operator, pipe up to 12 million litres a day of treated effluent to three data centres. Ranhill SAJ is the state's treated water utility and charges data centres RM5.33 per cubic metre.

authorities.name: Selangor State Government and Air Selangor
authorities.role: Selangor approves no data centre until TNB confirms power and Air Selangor, the state water utility, confirms water. Each project also needs federal task force clearance.

authorities.name: National Water Services Commission (SPAN)
authorities.role: The federal water regulator. Its September 2025 guidelines ask data centres to cool with reclaimed water or air-cooled systems that discharge no water.

authorities.name: Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (PETRA)
authorities.role: Runs CRESS, the scheme for buying green power over TNB's grid. Its access charge for firm supply fell to 14 sen per kWh for projects running by the end of 2028.

authorities.name: Ministry of Finance
authorities.role: Funds the DESAC tax incentives with MIDA. Budget 2027, due in early October 2026, is where any change to them would appear.

authorities.name: Personal Data Protection Commissioner
authorities.role: Enforces the personal data law, including transfers abroad. Malaysia sets no data localisation rule today.

authorities.name: Bank Negara Malaysia
authorities.role: The central bank. Its technology risk policy governs how banks and other financial institutions run their systems, including outsourced data centres.

MY.authorities_note: Ranked by how much each body decides whether a project gets built in Malaysia today.
authorities_also: Local councils approve building plans and the Department of Environment reviews environmental impact assessments under general law. No data centre specific rule from either was found.
MITI said in November 2025 that a single data centre licensing authority would be set up. No law or start date has been published.

SG.summary: Singapore controls data centre growth by handing out power in competitive government calls. The latest round in August 2026 gave 200MW at a new Jurong Island park to four operators, on condition that each site is highly efficient and draws at least half its power from green sources. A Digital Infrastructure Bill, first read in Parliament on 8 September 2026, would require a licence for every data centre of 3MW or more and is waiting for its Second Reading.

approvals.title: 2019 moratorium ended in 2022
approvals.text: Singapore paused new data centre approvals in 2019. The government lifted the pause in January 2022 and said it would choose only projects that are best in class for resource efficiency and that serve national economic goals.

sources.title: Singapore lifts data center moratorium - but sets conditions

approvals.title: Pilot DC-CFA allocated about 80MW
approvals.text: The pilot Data Centre Call for Application (DC-CFA) chose four proposals in July 2023 for about 80MW in total. The winners were the AirTrunk-ByteDance consortium, Equinix, GDS and Microsoft. Winning projects had to use liquid cooling widely and earn Green Mark for Data Centres Platinum certification.

sources.title: Four data centre proposals selected as part of pilot Data Centre Call for Application ("DC-CFA")

approvals.title: DC-CFA2 awarded 200MW on Jurong Island
approvals.text: The second call (DC-CFA2) received more than 20 proposals. It gave 50MW each to Digital Realty, Equinix, Keppel Data Centres and ST Telemedia Global Data Centres, 200MW in total, at the Jurong Island data centre park. The allocation is provisional.

sources.title: Four data centre proposals selected as part of second data centre - call for application ("DC-CFA2")
Singapore gov't allocates 200MW of power for four data center developers on Jurong Island

approvals.title: DC-CFA2 efficiency and green energy conditions
approvals.text: DC-CFA2 projects must reach a power usage effectiveness (PUE) of 1.25 or better at full IT load. PUE is total facility power divided by IT power. At least 50% of each project's power must come from approved green pathways such as biomethane, low-carbon ammonia or hydrogen, and each project must earn Green Mark for Data Centres 2024 Platinum.

sources.title: Launch of second data centre – Call for application

approvals.title: Green Data Centre Roadmap sets capacity path
approvals.text: The 2024 Green Data Centre Roadmap targets at least 300MW of additional data centre capacity in the near term. More capacity is tied to the use of green energy.

sources.title: Charting green growth pathways at scale for data centres in Singapore

approvals.title: Jurong Island low-carbon data centre park
approvals.text: The government has set aside about 20 hectares on Jurong Island for a data centre park of up to 700MW. Nearby energy projects such as solar, battery storage and hydrogen-ready plants are planned to support it.

sources.title: Singapore to host 700MW data center park on Jurong Island

approvals.title: Fire Code rules for large battery systems
approvals.text: Clause 10.3 of SCDF's Fire Code 2023 sets fire safety rules for energy storage systems above a stored energy threshold. The clause does not name data centres, but large lithium-ion UPS battery rooms may fall under it if they pass the threshold. SCDF revised the rules for aboveground systems from 1 March 2026 and for basement systems from 2 March 2025. Operators should confirm the scope with SCDF.

sources.title: Clause 10.3 Energy Storage Systems

power.title: Large users buy at wholesale prices
power.text: A business that uses 4MWh or more a month on average buys electricity at wholesale prices through SP Group unless it picks a licensed retailer. Large data centres therefore pay market-linked prices. They do not pay the regulated household tariff.

sources.title: Buying from a Retailer

power.title: Regulated tariff cut for Q4 2026
power.text: The regulated household tariff is 28.59 Singapore cents per kWh before GST from 1 October to 31 December 2026. That is 10.4% lower than the 31.91 cents charged in Q3. The overall tariff including non-household rates fell by an average of 10.6%.

sources.title: Electricity Tariff Revision for the Period 1 October to 31 December 2026
Singapore households to get 10.4pc electricity tariff cut from October as fuel costs ease

power.title: Low-carbon electricity import programme
power.text: Singapore aims to import about 6GW of low-carbon electricity by 2035. EMA had given conditional approvals for more than 8GW by February 2026. In August 2026 it approved a further 900MW of solar and battery power from Johor, expected around 2029.

sources.title: Singapore's Energy Transition: Progress, Security and Preparation
EMA Grants Conditional Approvals for 900 MW of Electricity Trade Between Peninsular Malaysia and Singapore

power.title: Carbon tax feeds into power prices
power.text: Power generators pay a carbon tax of S$45 per tonne of CO2 equivalent in 2026 and 2027. Generators pass this cost on through electricity prices, so data centres bear it indirectly.

sources.title: Singapore Will Raise Climate Ambition to Achieve Net Zero Emissions By or Around Mid Century, and Revises Carbon Tax Levels from 2024

power.title: PUE 1.3 goal for all data centres
power.text: The Green Data Centre Roadmap aims for data centres to reach a PUE of 1.3 or lower. This is a policy goal with no legal penalties attached. New capacity awarded in 2026 must meet the stricter 1.25.

sources.title: Charting green growth pathways at scale for data centres in Singapore
Data centre operators seek adequate time to meet green targets under new Bill

power.title: Green Mark for Data Centres 2024
power.text: BCA and IMDA run the Green Mark for Data Centres certification. It rates energy efficiency, sustainable design and maintainability at Gold, GoldPLUS or Platinum level. Platinum under the 2024 version is mandatory for DC-CFA2 winners.

sources.title: Launch of second data centre – Call for application

incentives.title: Resource Efficiency Grant for Emissions
incentives.text: EDB's Resource Efficiency Grant for Emissions, REG(E), can fund up to 50% of qualifying costs for data centre projects that cut emissions. A project must cut at least 250 tonnes of CO2 a year, verified by an independent endorser. EDB accepts applications until the end of FY2030.

sources.title: Resource Efficiency Grant for Emissions (REG(E))
Charting green growth pathways at scale for data centres in Singapore

incentives.title: Energy Efficiency Grant for data centres
incentives.text: IMDA's grant pays up to 70% of the cost of pre-approved efficient IT equipment for small firms and up to 30% for larger ones, capped at S$30,000 per firm. It is open only to groups with turnover of S$500 million or less, so large operators cannot use it. IMDA's page says these rates apply until 31 March 2026, and no extension has been confirmed.

sources.title: Energy Efficiency Grant for the Data Centre (DC) sector

incentives.title: Refundable Investment Credit
incentives.text: The Refundable Investment Credit can cover up to 50% of qualifying spending, and unused credits are paid out in cash within four years. EDB and EnterpriseSG run it. The scheme does not name data centres as a qualifying activity.

sources.title: Annex C-1: Refundable Investment Credit

data.title: PDPA transfer rule, no localisation
data.text: The Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) lets organisations move personal data abroad only if the data keeps protection comparable to the PDPA. The Act has no general rule that data must stay in Singapore.

sources.title: Advisory Guidelines on Key Concepts in the Personal Data Protection Act

data.title: MAS technology risk rules for banks
data.text: MAS Technology Risk Management Guidelines require financial institutions to manage cloud and third-party provider risk and to protect data confidentiality. They set no specific rule on where data must be stored.

sources.title: MAS Enhances Guidelines to Combat Heightened Cyber Risks

data.title: Government on Commercial Cloud
data.text: Government on Commercial Cloud (GCC) is GovTech's platform for running less sensitive government systems on commercial cloud. GovTech aimed to move more than 70% of eligible systems to the cloud by the end of 2022.

sources.title: Government on Commercial Cloud (GCC 2.0)

data.title: Cybersecurity Act data centre duties not started
data.text: The 2024 amendments to the Cybersecurity Act created a category called foundational digital infrastructure, covering cloud providers and data centres. The amendments on critical information infrastructure took effect on 31 October 2025. The part on foundational digital infrastructure had not started as of that date.

sources.title: CSA First Reading of the Cybersecurity (Amendment) Bill
Provisions in Singapore's Cybersecurity (Amendment) Act came into force on 31 October 2025

data.title: Security licence for large sites and clouds
data.text: The Digital Infrastructure Bill would license data centres of 10MW critical IT load or more that serve third parties. It would also license cloud providers that earn at least S$100 million a year from Singapore users. Licensees would need security, business continuity and incident reporting measures, with fines up to S$1 million or 10% of Singapore turnover, whichever is higher.

sources.title: New Digital Infrastructure Bill To Strengthen The Foundations For Singapore's Digital Economy
Singapore consults on new Digital Infrastructure Bill

water.title: PUB mandatory water efficiency practices
water.text: Under PUB's Mandatory Water Efficiency Management Practices, large water users such as data centres must report their water use to PUB.

sources.title: Navigating Singapore's Data Centre Regulatory Framework

water.title: WUE goal of 2.0 m3 per MWh
water.text: IMDA and PUB aim to help data centres reach a water usage effectiveness (WUE) of 2.0 cubic metres per MWh or lower over the next 10 years. WUE is the water a site uses for each unit of IT energy. This is a policy goal with no legal penalties attached.

sources.title: Navigating Singapore's Data Centre Regulatory Framework

water.title: PUB data centre water benchmark
water.text: PUB's sector benchmark puts the median data centre WUE at 2.1 cubic metres per MWh in its December 2025 edition. The previous figure was 2.2.

sources.title: Sectoral Water Efficiency Benchmark
Navigating Singapore's Data Centre Regulatory Framework

water.title: Tropical data centre standard SS 697
water.text: SS 697:2023 guides operators to raise data hall temperatures step by step to 26°C or higher. IMDA estimates 2% to 5% cooling energy savings for each 1°C rise. The standard is voluntary.

sources.title: Tropical Data Centre (DC) Standard
Charting green growth pathways at scale for data centres in Singapore

water.title: IT equipment efficiency standard SS 715
water.text: SS 715:2025 sets energy efficiency baselines for data centre IT equipment and calls for equipment that runs safely at up to 35°C. It aims to cut IT equipment energy use by at least 30%.

sources.title: Singapore IT energy efficiency standard for data centres launched

watching.title: Digital Infrastructure Bill Second Reading
watching.text: The Bill had its First Reading on 8 September 2026, after a public consultation from 1 to 22 July 2026 that drew 25 responses. MDDI said the Second Reading will happen at the next available sitting of Parliament. As of 3 October 2026 the Bill had not passed.

sources.title: New Digital Infrastructure Bill To Strengthen The Foundations For Singapore's Digital Economy
Public Consultation on the Digital Infrastructure Bill

watching.title: Sustainability licence for 3MW and above
watching.text: Under the Bill, every data centre operator with 3MW or more of critical IT load would need an IMDA licence and would have to meet facility PUE standards. Regulations will set the exact PUE level later. IT equipment and water efficiency rules may follow after industry consultation.

sources.title: New Digital Infrastructure Bill To Strengthen The Foundations For Singapore's Digital Economy

watching.title: Licences expected by mid-2027
watching.text: Major data centre operators and cloud providers are expected to hold licences by mid-2027, according to The Straits Times. Operators have asked for enough transition time to upgrade existing sites. MDDI has said existing data centres will get time to adjust.

sources.title: Data centre operators seek adequate time to meet green targets under new Bill

watching.title: Next capacity call under review
watching.text: After the DC-CFA2 awards, the government said it will review in 18 to 24 months whether another call is needed to allocate more capacity.

sources.title: Singapore gov't allocates 200MW of power for four data center developers on Jurong Island

watching.title: Carbon tax to rise by 2030
watching.text: The carbon tax is set to rise from S$45 per tonne to between S$50 and S$80 per tonne by 2030. Generators pass carbon costs on through electricity prices, so this would raise power costs for data centres.

sources.title: Singapore Will Raise Climate Ambition to Achieve Net Zero Emissions By or Around Mid Century, and Revises Carbon Tax Levels from 2024

Build and energisation timelines for the DC-CFA2 Jurong Island sites were not disclosed.
Details of the MAS Guidelines on Outsourcing were not reviewed.

authorities.name: Economic Development Board (EDB)
authorities.role: Runs the Data Centre Call for Application (DC-CFA) with IMDA. The call is the only route to new data centre capacity in Singapore. On 21 August 2026 the second call gave 50MW each to Digital Realty, Equinix, Keppel Data Centres and ST Telemedia, 200MW in total, at the Jurong Island park. EDB also runs the REG(E) emissions grant.

authorities.name: Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA)
authorities.role: Runs the DC-CFA with EDB and sets the Green Data Centre Roadmap, which targets 300MW more capacity and a PUE goal of 1.3. Under the Digital Infrastructure Bill, every operator with 3MW or more of critical IT load would need an IMDA licence and would have to meet PUE standards. The Bill had its First Reading on 8 September 2026.

authorities.name: Ministry of Digital Development and Information (MDDI)
match: Ministry of Digital Development and Information
authorities.role: Owns the Digital Infrastructure Bill, which had its First Reading on 8 September 2026. The Bill would add a security licence for third-party data centres of 10MW or more and for cloud providers earning S$100 million or more a year from Singapore users. Licensees would need security, business continuity and incident reporting measures.

authorities.name: Energy Market Authority (EMA)
authorities.role: Regulates the power sector and plans new generation and electricity imports. On 29 April 2026 it opened a tender for new hydrogen-ready gas units of at least 600MW each, due in 2031 and 2032, and named data centres as a driver of demand. In August 2026 it gave conditional approval for 900MW of imports from Johor.

authorities.name: JTC Corporation
authorities.role: Controls most industrial land. A data centre on JTC land needs JTC plan consent for major building works. The government set aside about 20 hectares on Jurong Island for a data centre park of up to 700MW, and the DC-CFA2 winners will build there.

authorities.name: Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA)
authorities.role: Zones the land and grants planning permission. Data centres count as industrial e-business uses. They are allowed in Business Park, Business 1 and Business 2 zones, subject to prior planning permission.

authorities.name: Building and Construction Authority (BCA)
authorities.role: Approves building plans before construction starts. It runs the Green Mark for Data Centres certification with IMDA. Platinum under the 2024 version is mandatory for DC-CFA2 winners.

authorities.name: PUB, Singapore's National Water Agency
authorities.role: Supplies water and must approve trade effluent before it is discharged into the public sewers. Data centres, as large water users, must report their water use and efficiency plans every year. PUB and IMDA aim for a water usage effectiveness of 2.0 cubic metres per MWh or lower.

authorities.name: SP Group
authorities.role: Runs the national grid and is the default supplier for large users. A business that uses 4MWh or more a month buys at wholesale prices through SP Group unless it picks a licensed retailer. Most large data centres therefore pay market-linked prices.

authorities.name: Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA)
authorities.role: Administers the Cybersecurity Act. The 2024 amendments created a category for foundational digital infrastructure that covers data centres and cloud providers. The duties for that category had not started as of October 2026.

authorities.name: Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF)
authorities.role: Approves fire safety works. Operators need SCDF approval before they carry out any fire safety works in a data centre building.

SG.authorities_note: Ranked by how much each body decides whether a project gets built in Singapore today.
authorities_also: The Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) lifted the 2019 to 2022 pause on new data centres and set the rule that only best-in-class projects are chosen.

The National Environment Agency (NEA) receives development control submissions for industrial developments and enforces emissions and waste standards. Its Energy Conservation Act sectors do not list data centres.
The Ministry of Finance and National Climate Change Secretariat (MOF and NCCS) set the carbon tax, S$45 per tonne in 2026 and 2027, which generators pass on through power prices.
The Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC) enforces the PDPA transfer rule, which has no general localisation duty.
The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) sets technology risk rules that banks apply when they choose cloud and data centre providers.
Enterprise Singapore publishes Singapore Standards with IMDA, including the voluntary tropical data centre standard SS 697.

ID.summary: Indonesia lets private companies host most data offshore, but banks, payment firms and government bodies must keep systems in the country. Power is the main constraint, and PLN, the state utility, is signing very large supply deals while grid tariffs have stayed flat through 2026. A new personal data regulation, PP 33/2026, takes effect on 16 January 2027 and sets rules for sending personal data abroad.

approvals.title: Data centres licensed under KBLI 63112
approvals.text: Data centre operators register under business code KBLI 63112, which covers hosting and related activities. The activity is rated medium to high risk, so an operator needs a business number (NIB) and a standard certificate through OSS, the online licensing system. Medium and large sites must sit in an industrial zone.
approvals.authority: Ministry of Investment and Downstreaming (BKPM) via OSS

sources.title: Apa Itu Data Center dan Bagaimana Perizinan Usahanya di Indonesia?

approvals.title: PP 28/2025 replaces old licensing rules
approvals.text: Government Regulation 28 of 2025 sets the current risk based licensing system and revoked PP 5/2021. It took effect on 5 June 2025 and links licensing to the updated KBLI 2025 business codes. Existing licences stay valid under the new codes.

sources.title: Penyelenggaraan Perizinan Berusaha Berbasis Risiko
Reformasi Perizinan Berusaha, PP 28/2025 Integrasikan OSS dan Penyesuaian KBLI 2025

approvals.title: Electronic system operator registration
approvals.text: Data centre and cloud businesses in the private sector must register as an electronic system operator, known as PSE. Registration is required before a system starts serving users under PP 71/2019.
approvals.authority: Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs (Komdigi)

sources.title: Apa Itu Data Center dan Bagaimana Perizinan Usahanya di Indonesia?
Peraturan Pemerintah Nomor 71 Tahun 2019

approvals.title: Full foreign ownership allowed
approvals.text: The data hosting business line under KBLI 63112 is open to foreign ownership up to 100 percent. Foreign owned companies still go through OSS and PSE registration.

sources.title: Data Center in Indonesia: Prospective Business Opportunities

approvals.title: Nongsa Digital Park special zone in Batam
approvals.text: Nongsa Digital Park in Batam is a special economic zone (KEK) set up by Government Regulation 68 of 2021. It covers 166 hectares and plans data centres. Firms there get licences through a single window run by the zone administrator.
approvals.authority: National Council for Special Economic Zones

sources.title: Nongsa Digital Park Targetkan Jadi Gerbang Ekonomi Digital Indonesia

approvals.title: National data centre still not running
approvals.text: The government built a National Data Centre (PDN) in Cikarang for state data, finished in March 2025. As of 15 December 2025 it had not started operations while it completed security requirements from BSSN, the cyber agency. A planned second site in Batam was dropped after loan talks with South Korea failed.

sources.title: PDN Belum Beroperasi, Komdigi: Masih Proses Pemenuhan Persyaratan
PDN Cikarang Sudah 99,74% Rampung, Begini Nasib PDN Batam

approvals.title: West Java halts a 640MW campus over permits
approvals.text: On 30 September 2026 West Java Governor Dedi Mulyadi stopped construction of BDx's 640MW AI campus at Jatiluhur in Purwakarta. Its environmental impact assessment (AMDAL) and building approval (PBG) had not been issued. He said the halt was over missing permits, with no environmental violation found. Construction had started on 22 September 2026.

sources.title: AMDAL dan PBG Belum Tuntas, Proyek Pusat Data AI Jatiluhur Disetop Sementara
West Java Freezes Work on BDx 640MW AI Data Center Campus Over Missing Environmental and Building Permits

power.title: Large industrial tariff at Rp 996.74 per kWh
power.text: PLN, the state utility, charges Rp 996.74 per kilowatt hour on the I-4 tariff for industrial users at 30,000 kVA and above. This rate still applied on 1 October 2026.
power.authority: Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (ESDM) and PLN

sources.title: Daftar Tarif Listrik yang Berlaku Per 1 Oktober 2026
Tarif Listrik PLN 1 Oktober 2026, Apakah Ada Kenaikan?

power.title: Tariffs held flat each quarter
power.text: The government sets tariffs every quarter and kept them unchanged in the first quarter of 2026 to protect purchasing power. As of 2 October 2026 no decision for the fourth quarter had been announced, so third quarter rates still applied.

sources.title: Tarif listrik dipastikan tidak naik, sampai kapan?
Tarif Listrik PLN 1 Oktober 2026, Apakah Ada Kenaikan?

power.title: Premium service tariffs for reliable supply
power.text: PLN offers premium service rates to customers who want higher reliability, under Energy Ministry Regulation 28 of 2016. The state auditor found PLN lost Rp 5.69 trillion in 2021 because these rates were not fully applied.

sources.title: PLN Reports Losses as Premium Tariffs Fail to Deliver

power.title: Batam runs on a separate utility
power.text: Batam is served by PLN Batam, which has its own tariff decision from the Energy Ministry. Its peak load is 841 MW in 2026 and is forecast to reach 2,540 MW by 2035. Data centres are expected to use more than half of Batam's peak load by 2029.
power.authority: ESDM, PLN Batam and BP Batam

sources.title: BP Batam dan PLN Siapkan Strategi Energi Hadapi Lonjakan Investasi Data Center
BP Batam pastikan keandalan energi dukung 1,47 GW data center

power.title: Renewable energy certificates from PLN
power.text: PLN sells renewable energy certificates (RECs), where each certificate stands for one megawatt hour of clean power. Buyers can claim renewable use without building their own plants. EDGE DC was the first Jakarta data centre to receive them in 2022.

sources.title: EDGE DC - the first data center in Jakarta receives REC from PLN

power.title: Rooftop solar without grid export credit
power.text: Energy Ministry Regulation 2 of 2024 governs rooftop solar on customer sites. Excess power sent to the grid no longer reduces bills, and PLN sets how much capacity can connect through a quota.

sources.title: Rapor Setahun Permen ESDM PLTS Atap, Iklim Usaha Dinilai Jadi Lebih Pasti

incentives.title: Special zone tax holiday tiers
incentives.text: Investors in core activities of a special economic zone can get a corporate tax holiday under Finance Ministry Regulation 130 of 2020. It runs 10 years for Rp 100 billion of investment, 15 years for Rp 500 billion and 20 years for Rp 1 trillion. Officials said the scheme was available to 31 December 2025.
incentives.authority: Ministry of Finance and National Council for Special Economic Zones

sources.title: Investor KEK Masih Bisa Nikmati Tax Holiday, Ini Syaratnya!

incentives.title: Tax holiday for 2026 capped by minimum tax
incentives.text: The Finance Ministry said the tax holiday continues in 2026 through a new regulation. Relief will only bring the rate down to the 15 percent global minimum tax, against a normal 22 percent rate.

sources.title: Kemenkeu Pastikan Tax Holiday Lanjut 2026 dengan Prinsip Pajak Minimum Global

incentives.title: Global minimum tax in force
incentives.text: Indonesia applies a 15 percent global minimum tax from tax year 2025 under Finance Ministry Regulation 136 of 2024. Large groups with an effective rate below 15 percent pay a top up tax, which reduces the value of tax holidays.

sources.title: Ada Pajak Minimum Global, RI Cari Cara Biar Insentif KEK Tetap Menarik

incentives.title: Special zone duty and VAT relief
incentives.text: Data centre investors in Nongsa Digital Park can get VAT exemption, waived import duty and import income tax, and 50 to 100 percent cuts in Batam local taxes. Non fiscal perks include licensing through the zone administrator and long stay visas.
incentives.authority: National Council for Special Economic Zones

sources.title: Pemerintah Tebar Insentif Ini Buat Tarik Investasi Bangun Data Center

incentives.title: Komdigi proposes data centre tax breaks
incentives.text: Komdigi proposed tax breaks for data centre providers and for customers importing equipment, plus simpler licensing. It also wants new sites spread beyond Jakarta and Batam.

sources.title: Komdigi Usul Ada Insentif Pajak dan Pangkas Regulasi demi Bisnis Data Center RI Tak Kalah Saing

data.title: Public sector data must stay onshore
data.text: Under PP 71/2019, public scope electronic system operators must manage, process and store their systems and data in Indonesia. Private scope operators may place systems abroad. PP 71/2019 replaced PP 82/2012.

sources.title: PP PSTE Dikhawatirkan Ganggu Kedaulatan Data

data.title: No private sector localisation mandate
data.text: In December 2023 the then communications minister said PP 71/2019 would not be revised. He said foreign companies are not required to put data centres in Indonesia.
data.authority: Ministry of Communication and Informatics (now Komdigi)

sources.title: Menkominfo: Perusahaan Asing Tak Wajib Lokalisasi Data Center di RI

data.title: Personal Data Protection Law
data.text: Law 27 of 2022 on personal data protection was enacted on 17 October 2022. Breaches must be reported to affected people within 3 times 24 hours, and fines reach 2 percent of annual revenue.

sources.title: Landasan Hukum Pelindungan Data Pribadi di Indonesia

data.title: PP 33/2026 implements the data law
data.text: Government Regulation 33 of 2026 sets the detailed rules for the personal data law and takes effect on 16 January 2027. Data may go abroad only where the destination has equal or higher protection, other safeguards apply, or the person consents. A data protection agency enforces it.

sources.title: Pemerintah Akhirnya Terbitkan Kerangka Implementasi Pelindungan Data Pribadi: Berlaku Mulai 16 Januari 2027

data.title: Banks must host systems in Indonesia
data.text: OJK regulation 11/POJK.03/2022, issued on 7 July 2022, requires banks to place systems in data centres and disaster recovery centres in Indonesia. Offshore placement needs prior approval from OJK, the financial regulator.

sources.title: Ada POJK Penyelenggara Teknologi Informasi, Pusat Data Diatur Ulang

data.title: Domestic payments processed onshore
data.text: Bank Indonesia regulation 22/23/PBI/2020 requires domestic payment transactions to be processed in Indonesia. This covers initiation, authorisation, clearing and settlement. It took effect on 1 July 2021.

sources.title: Peraturan Bank Indonesia Nomor 22/23/PBI/2020 tentang Sistem Pembayaran

water.title: No water efficiency benchmark for data centres
water.text: Indonesia covers data centre water use through general water permits and environmental impact assessments. There is no national efficiency benchmark specific to data centres, so projects are judged case by case.

sources.title: IESR Desak Aturan Khusus Data Center, Listrik 25 GW pada 2035 Jadi Sorotan

water.title: Batam lists water security as a priority
water.text: BP Batam, the authority that runs Batam, named water security as one of five priorities for data centre growth. The others are competitive power prices, supply guarantees, faster infrastructure and joint utility planning.

sources.title: BP Batam pastikan keandalan energi dukung 1,47 GW data center
Batam Kejar Pusat Data Center Regional, Energi Harus Siap

water.title: Batam requires data centres to make their own water
water.text: BP Batam chief and Batam Mayor Amsakar Achmad said data centres that need large volumes of water must build their own seawater desalination (SWRO) plants instead of drawing on public reservoirs. The policy targets the Nongsa special economic zone and the Kabil industrial area. Planned desalination capacity is about 750 litres a second within two to three years, rising to about 1,000.

sources.title: Batam Data Centers: BP Batam Requires Independent SWRO to Protect Public Water Supply
Batam residents protest data centers amid water crisis

watching.title: Fourth quarter 2026 tariff decision
watching.text: As of 2 October 2026 the government had not set electricity tariffs for October to December 2026. Third quarter rates apply until it does.

sources.title: Tarif Listrik PLN 1 Oktober 2026, Apakah Ada Kenaikan?

watching.title: Renewable energy bill and power wheeling
watching.text: Parliament aims to pass the New and Renewable Energy bill (RUU EBET) in 2026, a legislator said on 14 August 2026. The bill is expected to set rules for power wheeling, where a buyer uses PLN's grid to take power from a private renewable plant. Disputes over power wheeling stopped the bill in September 2024.

sources.title: DPR Targetkan RUU EBET Rampung 2026, Jadi Payung Hukum Transisi Energi
Tak Kunjung Disahkan, DPR Ungkap Nasib RUU EBET & Revisi UU Migas

watching.title: Energy minister pitches data centre power
watching.text: On 22 September 2026 Energy Minister Bahlil Lahadalia offered data centre projects to investors with competitive power prices and easier permits. PLN serves 159 data centres that used 2,378 GWh.

sources.title: Bahlil Tawarkan Proyek Pembangunan Data Center dengan Tarif Listrik Kompetitif

watching.title: Calls for national data centre rules
watching.text: On 1 October 2026 the think tank IESR urged dedicated data centre rules. It proposed closed loop cooling, PUE below 1.3 and renewable shares of 35 percent by 2030 and 50 percent by 2040. PUE measures total site power against IT power.

sources.title: IESR Desak Aturan Khusus Data Center, Listrik 25 GW pada 2035 Jadi Sorotan

watching.title: Sustainable data centre standard in drafting
watching.text: Komdigi is working with industry body IDPRO on a sustainable data centre standard covering power, connectivity and uptime. Komdigi said it is meant as a shared guide and will add no new regulation.

sources.title: Komdigi Fokus Selesaikan Standar Pusat Data Berkelanjutan Indonesia

watching.title: Danantara and Telkom plan 1 GW
watching.text: Telkom's data centre arm NeutraDC plans up to 1 GW of AI data centres with Danantara, the state investment fund, and PLN supplying power. Sites named include Batam, Greater Jakarta, Java and Manado.

sources.title: Bersama Danantara, TelkomGroup Siapkan Infrastruktur Data Center Menuju Sovereign AI Indonesia
Danantara eyes wider data center investment as demand surges

authorities.name: PLN
authorities.role: The state utility and the main constraint on any project. It decides grid supply, sells the I-4 large industrial tariff and renewable energy certificates, and is signing very large supply deals. PLN Batam runs Batam's separate grid.

authorities.name: Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (ESDM)
authorities.role: Sets electricity tariffs every quarter and has held them flat through 2026. It sets the rooftop solar rules and is pitching data centre power to investors.

authorities.name: Provincial and regency governments
authorities.role: They hold the environmental impact assessment (AMDAL) and building approval (PBG) a site needs before it builds. West Java's governor stopped a 640MW campus at Jatiluhur on 30 September 2026 because both were missing.

authorities.name: Ministry of Investment and Downstreaming (BKPM)
authorities.role: Licenses every operator through OSS, the online licensing system. Data centres need a business number and a standard certificate, and medium and large sites must sit in an industrial zone. Full foreign ownership is allowed.

authorities.name: BP Batam and the National Council for Special Economic Zones
match: National Council for Special Economic Zones
authorities.role: BP Batam runs Batam, the main data centre market outside Jakarta, and now requires data centres that need large volumes of water to build their own seawater desalination plants. The council oversees special economic zones such as Nongsa Digital Park, where firms get tax relief and licences through one window.

authorities.name: Ministry of Communication and Digital Affairs (Komdigi)
authorities.role: Registers every electronic system operator and enforces the rule that public sector data stays in Indonesia. It runs the National Data Centre and has proposed tax breaks for data centres.

authorities.name: Ministry of Environment
authorities.role: Reviews environmental impact assessments and water permits. Indonesia has no water benchmark for data centres, so each project is judged case by case.

authorities.name: Financial Services Authority (OJK)
authorities.role: Requires banks to host their systems and disaster recovery in Indonesia. Offshore placement needs its prior approval.

authorities.name: Bank Indonesia
authorities.role: Requires domestic payment transactions to be processed in Indonesia.

authorities.name: Ministry of Finance
authorities.role: Grants tax holidays. From 2026 relief can only bring the rate down to the 15 percent global minimum tax.

authorities.name: House of Representatives (DPR)
authorities.role: Is working on the renewable energy bill. The bill is expected to set rules for power wheeling, where a buyer takes private renewable power over PLN's grid.

ID.authorities_note: Ranked by how much each body decides whether a project gets built in Indonesia today.
authorities_also: Law 27 of 2022 and PP 33/2026 provide for a data protection agency to enforce the personal data rules. Its role for data centres is not yet set.

TH.summary: Thailand has frozen its data centre pipeline while it rewrites the rules. On 4 September 2026 a new Cabinet-level board paused construction on 49 projects and froze approvals for 117 more. New standards on building definition, zoning, power tariffs, water and fuel storage are being finalised in October 2026. Until those standards are approved and published, no new project should expect permits, utility connections or BOI approval.

approvals.title: National Data Center Business Policy Committee created
approvals.text: The Cabinet approved a Prime Minister's Office regulation on 5 August 2026 setting up a national committee to oversee data centre investment. Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas chairs it. It is the first body with authority over data centres across all ministries.
approvals.authority: Cabinet / Office of the Prime Minister

sources.title: BOI รื้อเกณฑ์ Data Center ชู 4 มิติดันไทยสู่ฮับ AI ยั่งยืน คุมเข้มใช้พลังงาน ทรัพยากรน้ำ พร้อมตอบโจทย์ชาติ และการจ้างงานไทย
Thailand pauses 166 data centre projects to rewrite rules

approvals.title: 49 projects paused and 117 approvals frozen
approvals.text: At its first meeting on 4 September 2026 the committee paused construction on 49 data centres and froze approval of 117 more, which is 166 projects in total. It gave four subcommittees one month to write minimum standards. They cover economic benefit, infrastructure, sites and buildings, and environment. The pause followed an unlicensed diesel storage and leak incident at a Rama 9 data centre in Bangkok.
approvals.authority: National Data Center Business Policy Committee

sources.title: Thailand pauses 166 data centre projects to rewrite rules
บอร์ดดาต้าเซ็นเตอร์นัดแรกขีดเส้น 1 เดือนออกระเบียบเกณฑ์คุมน้ำ-ไฟ-ผังเมือง สั่งรวมข้อมูลภายใน 1 สัปดาห์ พร้อมตั้ง 4 อนุกรรมการ
Thailand data center suspension traced to diesel spillage from Bangkok facility as one of the causes

approvals.title: Data centres get their own building category
approvals.text: On 1 October 2026 the committee approved a separate legal definition for data centre buildings. Until now they were classed as large buildings, and some were permitted as warehouses or offices. Five size classes based on power use will set rules on safety, structure, water reserves and backup fuel tanks. The Department of Public Works and Town and Country Planning is finalising the technical rules, and the changes go to Cabinet within about a month.
approvals.authority: National Data Center Business Policy Committee / Ministry of Interior

sources.title: Thailand approves separate legal definition of data centre buildings
บอร์ดดาต้าเซ็นเตอร์เคาะ 5 ประเภท แบ่งค่าไฟ 2 เรท พลังงานสะอาดถูกกว่าก๊าซ

approvals.title: BOI four-pillar screening and energy subcommittee
approvals.text: BOI now screens data centre projects on four pillars. These are benefit to Thailand, energy security, water, and environment and zoning. Since July 2026 applicants need approval from a new subcommittee on energy management and data centre screening. This also applies to promoted projects that add more than 30% IT load. This replaced the ERC grid-capacity letter that had been required for new applications from 30 March 2026.

sources.title: Thailand: Updated BOI Requirement for Data Centers
Thailand: New Thailand BOI Data Center Investment Requirement

approvals.title: Draft digital infrastructure law with licensing
approvals.text: A draft bill would require data centre operators to hold a licence from the Minister of Digital Economy and Society and to be Thai-registered companies. It would require an environmental impact assessment (EIA), siting in factory-zoned areas, and own water and power sources for large sites. Unlicensed operation could bring up to 5 years in prison. The public hearing runs 3 September 2026 to 15 October 2026, and the size thresholds are left to later regulations.
approvals.authority: Ministry of Digital Economy and Society (DES)

sources.title: ชำแหละร่าง พ.ร.บ.โครงสร้างพื้นฐานดิจิทัล คุมดาต้าเซ็นเตอร์
Thai bill to require environmental impact assessment for data centres

approvals.title: 50% Thai content rule for licensed operators
approvals.text: Proposed conditions would require at least 50% of structural materials, construction work and electrical systems to come from Thai makers where supply, standards and price allow. They would apply to data centre operators seeking telecom licences, and existing operators would get 90 days to comply. NESDC said the rules should be in force by mid-October 2026.
approvals.authority: NBTC / National Data Center Business Policy Committee

sources.title: คุม'ดาต้าเซ็นเตอร์' ล็อกใช้ของไทย 50% คาดประกาศใช้ไม่เกินกลาง ต.ค.69

approvals.title: Bangkok inspections and permit freeze
approvals.text: The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) counted 49 data centres in the city, most under 2MW and inside office buildings. It runs random checks on building standards, fuel, water, heat, noise and fire safety. It has suspended new data centre permit applications until national guidelines are issued. The Interior Ministry told utilities to hold water and power connections for unapproved new projects.
approvals.authority: Bangkok Metropolitan Administration / Ministry of Interior

sources.title: Bangkok intensifies data centre inspections pending new guidelines
บอร์ดดาต้าเซ็นเตอร์นัดแรกขีดเส้น 1 เดือนออกระเบียบเกณฑ์คุมน้ำ-ไฟ-ผังเมือง สั่งรวมข้อมูลภายใน 1 สัปดาห์ พร้อมตั้ง 4 อนุกรรมการ

approvals.title: Diesel storage above 15,000 litres needs a permit
approvals.text: Under the Fuel Control Act 1999, storing more than 15,000 litres of fuel needs a permit. The Rama 9 facility allegedly held about 200,000 litres without one, and a criminal complaint was filed. Penalties are up to two years in prison or a fine up to 200,000 THB.

sources.title: Bangkok data centre faces charges over illegal fuel storage

power.title: Data centres become a separate tariff class
power.text: On 15 July 2026 the National Energy Policy Council (NEPC) meeting 2/2569 approved a separate electricity tariff class for data centres, called category 9. The rate is meant to be higher than other groups so households do not carry the cost. The Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) has not yet set the rate. Press reports have floated 5 to 6 THB per kWh, and this figure is unconfirmed.

sources.title: กพช.แยกค่าไฟสาธารณะพ้นบิลประชาชน เคาะใช้ไม่เกิน 200 หน่วย จ่าย 3 บาท
Thailand tightens data centre rules as AI boom strains power grid

power.title: Two data centre rates by power source
power.text: On 1 October 2026 the data centre committee agreed a two-rate design. Sites using clean energy or Direct PPAs would pay less than sites drawing gas-fired grid power. A subcommittee meets on 6 October 2026 to set the rate details.
power.authority: National Data Center Business Policy Committee / Ministry of Energy

Thailand approves separate legal definition of data centre buildings

power.title: Ft charge for September to December 2026
power.text: Ft is the automatic fuel adjustment charge added to every unit of power. ERC set Ft at 16.23 satang per unit for September to December 2026. The average tariff fell to about 3.89 THB per unit. Data centres pay industrial rates above 3 THB per unit until their own class takes effect.

sources.title: กกพ.หั่นค่าไฟ ก.ย.เหลือ 3.89 บาท ตัดไฟถนน 6 สตางค์ 200 หน่วยแรกไม่เกิน 3 บาท
จับตา ‘ค่าไฟ Data Center’ กกพ.เตรียมเคาะกติกาใหม่ เปิดทาง Direct PPA-ไฟสีเขียว

power.title: Direct PPA 2,000MW cap scrapped
power.text: A Direct PPA lets a user buy renewable power straight from a generator over the state grid, which is called third-party access. The pilot began with 2,000MW reserved for data centres. In August 2026 NEPC removed the cap and opened direct clean power purchases to all industries.

sources.title: Thailand Scraps Data Centre Power Cap, Opens Clean Electricity Market to All Industry
Thailand tightens data centre rules as AI boom strains power grid

power.title: Grid-use security deposit of 4.5m THB per MW
power.text: ERC plans a deposit of 4.5 million THB per MW to stop speculative capacity bookings. Half would be returned when a site uses 50% of planned power within a year, and all of it at 70%. The measure was awaiting Cabinet approval and is not yet confirmed as in force.

sources.title: ประกันใช้ไฟ 4.5 ล้าน/เมกะวัตต์ สกัดดาต้าเซ็นเตอร์ 7.3 แสนล้านลงทุนทิพย์
Thailand tightens data centre rules as AI boom strains power grid

power.title: 60% clean power minimum and new ERC licence
power.text: The Energy Ministry set four power criteria for data centres. They include a clean energy share of at least 60% in line with the new power plan, plus safety rules for backup batteries and diesel generators. Separately, ERC proposed a licence for selling power to data centres, with its hearing open 19 September 2026 to 18 October 2026.

sources.title: ก.พลังงาน เปิด 4 เกณฑ์คุมไฟ Data Center แยกอัตราเฉพาะ
Thailand: ERC Proposes Data Center Licensing

power.title: Utility Green Tariff programme
power.text: The Utility Green Tariff (UGT) lets large users buy certified renewable power from the state utilities. UGT1 launched in January 2025 with a premium of 0.0594 THB per unit. UGT2 adds a choice of specific solar or wind sources.

sources.title: Thailand introduces its first green electricity tariff – UGT1

incentives.title: BOI tax holidays of 5 or 8 years
incentives.text: Since 1 July 2025 BOI grants an 8-year corporate income tax exemption to high-efficiency data centres and 5 years to others. Both are capped at 100% of investment. High efficiency is judged on PUE (power usage effectiveness), water efficiency and benefits to Thailand such as training and local supply chains.

sources.title: Data Center Investments under Thailand’s Updated Incentive Criteria

incentives.title: Incentive review ordered in August 2026
incentives.text: The Deputy Prime Minister told BOI to review data centre incentives. The review weighs water, power, environment and real benefit to Thai citizens. He also said large operators should build their own power plants. No revised incentive package has been published.

sources.title: 'เอกนิติ' สั่ง BOI เร่งทบทวนสิทธิประโยชน์ 'ดาต้าเซ็นเตอร์' คุมน้ำไฟ-เน้นประโยชน์ชาติ

incentives.title: BOI pipeline of 42 promoted projects
incentives.text: BOI has promoted 42 data centre projects from 2024 to 2026 with 3,400MW of IT load and about 750 billion THB of investment. Press reports say BOI has made no new data centre approvals since April 2026 while the rules are rewritten.

sources.title: BOI รื้อเกณฑ์ Data Center ชู 4 มิติดันไทยสู่ฮับ AI ยั่งยืน คุมเข้มใช้พลังงาน ทรัพยากรน้ำ พร้อมตอบโจทย์ชาติ และการจ้างงานไทย

data.title: PDPA cross-border transfer rules
data.text: Two notifications under sections 28 and 29 of the Personal Data Protection Act took effect on 24 March 2024. Personal data may leave Thailand to destinations with adequate protection or under safeguards such as binding corporate rules, standard contract clauses or certification. They impose no general data localisation rule.

sources.title: Thailand Unveils Regulations for Cross-Border Personal Data Transfer

data.title: Proposed localisation of Thai personal data
data.text: The draft digital infrastructure bill would require personal data of Thai people and Thai corporate data to stay in Thailand by default. Exceptions would be set in ministerial regulations. The hearing closes 15 October 2026.
data.authority: Ministry of Digital Economy and Society (DES)

sources.title: ชำแหละร่าง พ.ร.บ.โครงสร้างพื้นฐานดิจิทัล คุมดาต้าเซ็นเตอร์
Thai bill to require environmental impact assessment for data centres

data.title: Go Cloud First and government data classes
data.text: Under the Cabinet's Go Cloud First policy, government agencies must prefer cloud for new IT projects. Draft guidelines from the Digital Government Development Agency (DGA) sort government data into three classes. The most sensitive class must stay in sovereign or state-controlled clouds in Thailand. The guidelines were in draft at the August 2025 hearing, and their final status is unconfirmed.

sources.title: Thailand Releases Draft Guidelines on Government Cloud Adoption and Data Classification

data.title: NCSA cloud security standard in force
data.text: The National Cyber Security Agency (NCSA) cloud security standard took effect on 10 September 2026. It covers government agencies, critical information infrastructure (CII) operators and the cloud providers that serve them. Systems must be classed by impact level and certified against minimum controls.

sources.title: Thailand’s Cloud Security Standard Is Now in Force: What Providers and CII Operators Must Review

data.title: Cybersecurity Act amendment on CII suppliers
data.text: A draft amendment to the Cybersecurity Act would make CII operators police their outside service providers. Providers would get a 60-day window to fix problems, and non-compliant providers would be listed. Cloud and data centre suppliers to CII would face these duties through their contracts.

sources.title: Thailand: Draft Amendment to the Cybersecurity Act

water.title: Water plans required from operators
water.text: ERC's proposed screening framework requires data centre operators to submit water management plans. BOI also screens water source, cooling technology, recycling and drought planning.

sources.title: Thailand tightens data centre rules as AI boom strains power grid
BOI รื้อเกณฑ์ Data Center ชู 4 มิติดันไทยสู่ฮับ AI ยั่งยืน คุมเข้มใช้พลังงาน ทรัพยากรน้ำ พร้อมตอบโจทย์ชาติ และการจ้างงานไทย

water.title: Large sites to use their own water
water.text: The draft digital infrastructure bill would require data centres above a set size to secure their own water sources. They could not draw on public supply. The size threshold is not yet defined.
water.authority: Ministry of Digital Economy and Society (DES)

sources.title: ชำแหละร่าง พ.ร.บ.โครงสร้างพื้นฐานดิจิทัล คุมดาต้าเซ็นเตอร์

water.title: EEC water demand estimate
water.text: The Royal Irrigation Department estimates the 16 BOI-approved data centres in the Eastern Economic Corridor (EEC) will need 42.4 to 50 million cubic metres of water a year. It is planning supply with the Office of the National Water Resources.

sources.title: กรมชลฯ กางแผนรับดาต้าเซ็นเตอร์ EEC ประเมิน ใช้น้ำปีละ 50 ล้าน ลบ.ม.

water.title: Community opposition in Ban Chang, Rayong
water.text: Residents in Ban Chang, Rayong, in the EEC have opposed data centre projects over water and power use. One developer responded with public forums and a joint monitoring model. Its water supply is about 35% municipal and 65% private sources.

sources.title: เปิดโมเดล Data Center อยู่ร่วมชุมชน ‘บ้านฉาง’ สกัดปัญหาพื้นที่ EEC

water.title: Eastwater supplies water in the EEC
water.text: Eastwater Stecon Utilities, a Thai water utility, signed a 10-year agreement to supply Bridge Data Centres' QH101 campus in Chonburi from May 2026. The campus is planned at up to 200MW.

sources.title: Bridge DC secures 'sustainable' water supply for upcoming data center campus in Chonburi, Thailand

watching.title: Data centre tariff rate decision
watching.text: A subcommittee meets on 6 October 2026 to set details of the two data centre electricity rates. ERC must then set and announce the category 9 rate.

sources.title: บอร์ดดาต้าเซ็นเตอร์เคาะ 5 ประเภท แบ่งค่าไฟ 2 เรท พลังงานสะอาดถูกกว่าก๊าซ

watching.title: Minimum standards due mid-October
watching.text: NESDC said the new data centre rules should be final by mid-October 2026. Under the draft, sites of 100MW or more would count as hyperscale and industrial-type sites would go in industrial estates. The one-month deadline from 4 September 2026 has passed without published standards. On 1 October 2026 officials said subcommittee criteria would be done within about a week.
watching.authority: NESDC / National Data Center Business Policy Committee

sources.title: Thailand set to finalize new data center regulations by mid-October - report
Thailand approves separate legal definition of data centre buildings

watching.title: Cabinet vote on building definition
watching.text: The new data centre building category and the five size classes go to Cabinet within about a month of 1 October 2026. A transition period for existing operators is promised, and its length is not yet set.

sources.title: Thailand approves separate legal definition of data centre buildings

watching.title: Public hearings closing in October
watching.text: The hearing on the draft digital infrastructure bill closes on 15 October 2026. The hearing on ERC's data centre power licence closes on 18 October 2026.

sources.title: ชำแหละร่าง พ.ร.บ.โครงสร้างพื้นฐานดิจิทัล คุมดาต้าเซ็นเตอร์
Thailand: ERC Proposes Data Center Licensing

watching.title: ERC data centre power rules by year end
watching.text: ERC plans to finish its full set of rules on selling power to data centres by the end of 2026. These cover grid supply, green power, Direct PPA and possible on-site generation, and ERC will present them to the data centre committee.

sources.title: จับตา ‘ค่าไฟ Data Center’ กกพ.เตรียมเคาะกติกาใหม่ เปิดทาง Direct PPA-ไฟสีเขียว

No final category 9 data centre tariff rate has been set or gazetted. The 5 to 6 THB per kWh figure appears only in press reports.

Specific setback distances from hospitals and housing in the new standards were not found.
Current EIA thresholds that would capture data centres were not found. The draft bill leaves its thresholds to later regulations.
The Interior Ministry inspection results for existing buildings could not be read. A Thairath report said checks were due by 2026-09-12, and the page was blocked.
No confirmation was found that the 4.5 million THB per MW deposit has been approved by Cabinet.

Final adoption of the DGA government cloud data classification guidelines was not confirmed.

authorities.name: National Data Center Business Policy Committee
match: National Data Center Business Policy Committee
Cabinet / Office of the Prime Minister
authorities.role: The top authority over data centres since August 2026, chaired by the Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister. It paused 49 projects and froze 117 approvals on 4 September 2026. Its four subcommittees are writing the minimum standards every project will have to meet, and Cabinet votes on its main decisions.

authorities.name: Board of Investment (BOI)
authorities.role: Grants the corporate tax holidays most large projects are planned around. It screens each project on benefit to Thailand, energy, water, and environment and zoning. Press reports say it has approved no new data centre since April 2026.

authorities.name: Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC)
authorities.role: Sets electricity rates and power licences. It must still set the data centre tariff rate, has proposed a licence for selling power to data centres and a grid deposit per MW, and plans its full set of data centre power rules by the end of 2026.

authorities.name: Ministry of Energy and the National Energy Policy Council (NEPC)
authorities.role: Set energy policy above the ERC. They created the data centre tariff class, opened direct renewable power purchases to all industries and proposed a 60% clean power minimum for data centres.

authorities.name: EGAT, MEA and PEA
authorities.role: The state utilities that physically connect a site and sell the green tariff. EGAT runs generation and the national grid. MEA distributes power in Bangkok, Nonthaburi and Samut Prakan, and PEA everywhere else. The Interior Ministry has told utilities to hold power and water connections for unapproved new projects.

authorities.name: Water utilities (MWA, PWA and Eastwater)
match: Bangkok Metropolitan Administration / Ministry of Interior
authorities.role: A site cannot run without a water connection, and the Interior Ministry has told utilities to hold connections for unapproved new projects. The Metropolitan Waterworks Authority (MWA) serves Bangkok, Nonthaburi and Samut Prakan, and the Provincial Waterworks Authority (PWA) most other areas. In the EEC, Eastwater Stecon Utilities signed a 10-year supply deal with Bridge Data Centres' Chonburi campus.

authorities.name: Ministry of Interior and local permit offices
authorities.role: Issue building permits and set the building code. The ministry is writing the new data centre building category. The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration has suspended new data centre permit applications in the city.

authorities.name: Ministry of Digital Economy and Society (DES)
match: Ministry of Digital Economy and Society (DES)
authorities.role: Drafted the digital infrastructure bill. If passed, every operator would need a DES licence and would have to be a Thai-registered company. Large sites would need an environmental impact assessment and their own water and power, and Thai data would stay in Thailand by default.

authorities.name: Department of Energy Business
authorities.role: Licenses fuel storage above 15,000 litres. The unlicensed diesel found at a Bangkok data centre in September 2026, which led to the national pause, fell under this permit.

authorities.name: NBTC
authorities.role: The telecom regulator. It has proposed that operators holding telecom licences source at least 50% of structural materials, construction work and electrical systems from Thai makers.

authorities.name: Personal Data Protection Committee (PDPC)
authorities.role: Enforces the personal data law, including the conditions for sending personal data abroad. Thailand has no general data localisation requirement today.

authorities.name: National Cyber Security Agency (NCSA)
authorities.role: Sets cyber security standards. Since 10 September 2026 its cloud security standard binds government agencies, critical infrastructure operators and the cloud providers that serve them.

authorities.name: Digital Government Development Agency (DGA)
authorities.role: Runs the government's Go Cloud First policy. Its draft data classes would keep the most sensitive government data in sovereign or state-controlled clouds in Thailand.

authorities.name: Royal Irrigation Department
authorities.role: Plans water supply for data centres in the Eastern Economic Corridor (EEC) with the Office of the National Water Resources. It estimates the 16 BOI-approved EEC sites will need 42.4 to 50 million cubic metres of water a year.

TH.authorities_note: Ranked by how much each body decides whether a project gets built in Thailand today.
authorities_also: The Office of Natural Resources and Environmental Policy and Planning (ONEP) reviews environmental impact assessments. Current thresholds that would capture a data centre were not found.
The Industrial Estate Authority of Thailand (IEAT) and the EEC Office control industrial estate land. The draft standards would place industrial-type data centres in industrial estates.
The Department of Industrial Works issues factory licences. No data centre requirement from it was found.

VN.summary: Vietnam's biggest open question for data centres is the electricity tariff. The power ministry told EVN in April 2026 to bill data centres at the cheaper production rate, yet the State Audit Office and EVN Ho Chi Minh City still apply the business rate and have pursued about 11.35 billion dong in arrears. Foreign investors face no ownership cap on data centre services, and new laws since January 2026 add tax breaks for AI data centres alongside tighter data storage and transfer rules.

approvals.title: No foreign ownership cap on data centres
approvals.text: The Telecommunications Law 2023 lets investors in data centre and cloud services hold any share of the business. Many other telecom services keep a 49% foreign ownership ceiling.

sources.title: Bỏ giới hạn sở hữu nước ngoài tại các trung tâm dữ liệu

approvals.title: Data centre services need a registration certificate
approvals.text: A company must register and receive a telecom service registration certificate before it sells data centre services. Decree 163/2024 sets the conditions, which include a technical plan and information security measures. Registration is lighter than a full telecom licence.
approvals.authority: Government; Ministry of Science and Technology

sources.title: Bộ TT&TT yêu cầu doanh nghiệp đăng ký, thông báo với 03 dịch vụ viễn thông mới

approvals.title: Provinces now handle many telecom procedures
approvals.text: Decree 133/2025 moved several telecom licensing and registration tasks to provincial People's Committees. Lawyers report that data centre registration certificates are now issued at provincial level.

sources.title: Nhiều nhiệm vụ lĩnh vực viễn thông được phân cấp, phân quyền cho UBND cấp tỉnh
