approvals.title: Mandatory technical standards before operation
approvals.text: Circular 42/2025 requires data centres to meet TCVN 9250:2021, TIA 942 or Uptime Institute tier standards. Operators self assess and declare conformity before launch, and report changes to the provincial science department within 15 days. Small edge sites are excluded.

sources.title: Thông tư 42/2025/TT-BKHCN: Tiêu chuẩn kỹ thuật cho trung tâm dữ liệu từ 2026

approvals.title: Faster investment route in tech zones
approvals.text: The Investment Law 2025 lets investors choose a special investment procedure for projects in high tech zones, digital technology zones and industrial zones. The investor files a written commitment to meet standards in place of several upfront approvals.

sources.title: 8 điểm mới của Luật Đầu tư 2025 từ 01/3/2026

approvals.title: Hi-tech park board approves CMC data centre
approvals.text: The Saigon Hi-Tech Park Management Board approved CMC Corporation as investor for a data centre in the Ho Chi Minh City Hi-Tech Park in July 2025. The project costs 6,260 billion dong, about US$250 million, and plans 3,000 racks and 30 MW of IT load. It runs in four phases from 2026 to 2030, with phase one due to operate by Q2 2027.

sources.title: CMC được chấp thuận là nhà đầu tư trung tâm dữ liệu 6.260 tỷ đồng tại TP.HCM

power.title: Circular 60 puts data centres on business tariff
power.text: Circular 60/2025 lists facilities that provide central data processing, storage and management services under the retail tariff for business use. Press reports cite Article 11 item 19. The old Circular 16/2014 had no data centre category, so data centres were billed at the cheaper production rate.

sources.title: Thông tư 60/2025/TT-BCT thực hiện giá bán điện mới nhất
Trả lời báo chí về giá bán lẻ điện cho trung tâm dữ liệu

power.title: Ministry letter directs production tariff
power.text: Dispatch 2818, dated 22 April 2026, told EVN to bill the technical systems of data centres at the production rate. Offices and other service areas stay on the business rate. Operators said the business tariff had raised power costs by more than 50%.

sources.title: EVN phải áp giá bán điện cho trung tâm dữ liệu theo đúng quy định
Giá điện cho các trung tâm dữ liệu - Bài toán mới của ngành điện Việt Nam

power.title: Auditor and EVN HCMC keep business rate
power.text: The State Audit Office told EVN Ho Chi Minh City to apply the business rate under Circular 60 and said Dispatch 2818 is guidance without legal force. EVN Ho Chi Minh City billed Viettel and CMC at the business rate and threatened supply cuts over 11.35 billion dong in arrears as of 16 September 2026.

power.title: Retail power prices can move quarterly
power.text: Decree 278/2026 amends Decree 72/2025 on how EVN adjusts the average retail power price. Adjustments must be at least three months apart. A rise below 2% or a fall below 1% triggers no change.
power.authority: Government; Ministry of Industry and Trade; EVN

Quy định mới nhất về thời gian điều chỉnh giá bán lẻ điện bình quân

power.title: Direct power purchase opened to data centres
power.text: Decree 57/2025 lets large users buy renewable power directly from generators, known as a direct power purchase agreement or DPPA. Decree 243/2026 amended it and names data centres among large users that can buy at 22 kV and above.
power.authority: Government; Ministry of Industry and Trade

sources.title: Đã có Nghị định 243/2026/NĐ-CP sửa cơ chế mua bán điện trực tiếp tại Nghị định 57

power.title: National data centre power plan ordered
power.text: Resolution 262/NQ-CP of 5 September 2026 tells the power ministry to prepare a power supply plan for data centres and high performance computing to 2030. The task missed its 15 August deadline and moved to September 2026.
power.authority: Government; Ministry of Industry and Trade

sources.title: Điện cho trung tâm dữ liệu lỡ hạn 15/8, dời mốc hoàn thành sang tháng 9
Nghị quyết 262/NQ-CP 2026 phiên họp Chính phủ thường kỳ tháng 8

incentives.title: Digital industry law lists data centres
incentives.text: The Law on Digital Technology Industry 2025 names data centres as shared digital infrastructure the state will prioritise. Projects in concentrated digital technology zones can get land rent cuts and corporate income tax benefits.

sources.title: 8 điểm đáng chú ý tại Luật Công nghiệp công nghệ số 2025

incentives.title: Direct state support for AI data centres
incentives.text: Article 28 of the same law allows direct support from local budgets for infrastructure and equipment in AI data centre construction. The law sets no percentage or cap for this support.

sources.title: Dự án chip bán dẫn và trung tâm dữ liệu AI được hỗ trợ trực tiếp chi phí đầu tư

incentives.title: Corporate tax break for AI data centres
incentives.text: Income from a new AI data centre project can be taxed at 10% for 15 years. It can also get four years of tax exemption and a 50% cut for the next nine years. The basis is the Corporate Income Tax Law 2025 and Decree 320/2025.

sources.title: Xây dựng trung tâm dữ liệu AI được ưu đãi thuế TNDN thế nào?

data.title: New cybersecurity decree replaces Decree 53
data.text: Decree 333/2026 implements the Cybersecurity Law 2025 and replaces Decree 53/2022. Covered domestic and foreign service providers must store Vietnamese users' data such as account names, payment details and IP addresses in Vietnam. Foreign firms get 12 months from a ministry notice to comply.

sources.title: Đã có Nghị định 333/2026/NĐ-CP quy định chi tiết và biện pháp thi hành Luật An ninh mạng
Decree No. 333/2026/ND-CP dated August 19, 2026 of the Government detailing a number of articles and measures for implementation of the Law on Cybersecurity

data.title: Cybersecurity Law 2025 now in force
data.text: Law 116/2025/QH15 merges the 2015 network information security law and the 2018 Cybersecurity Law. It keeps the duty to store user data in Vietnam and requires logs to be kept for at least 12 months.
data.authority: National Assembly; Ministry of Public Security

data.title: Personal Data Protection Law in force
data.text: Law 91/2025/QH15 governs personal data. A company that sends personal data abroad must file a transfer impact assessment with the Ministry of Public Security within 60 days of the first transfer. Fines for unlawful transfers reach 5% of prior year revenue.
data.authority: National Assembly; Ministry of Public Security

sources.title: Khung pháp lý chuyển dữ liệu xuyên biên giới của Việt Nam: Góc nhìn từ Luật Dữ liệu 2024 và Luật Bảo vệ Dữ liệu Cá nhân 2025

data.title: Decree 356 guides personal data law
data.text: Decree 356/2025 replaced Decree 13/2023 and took effect with the new law. Firms that provide data processing services do not get the small business exemption from impact assessments.

data.title: Data Law controls core and important data
data.text: The Data Law 2024 covers all digital data. Transfers of core or important data abroad need an impact assessment and a risk report to the Ministry of Public Security.
data.authority: National Assembly; Ministry of Public Security

data.title: Data analytics providers must notify first
data.text: Decree 347/2026 requires firms offering data analysis and data synthesis services to notify the National Data Centre before they operate. They must also file an annual report by 20 December.

water.title: Voluntary PUE and WUE standards exist
water.text: Vietnam has national standards in the TCVN 14285 series for data centre efficiency. Part 2 covers power usage effectiveness, or PUE, the ratio of total site energy to IT energy. Part 9 covers water usage effectiveness. These standards are voluntary.

sources.title: TCVN 14285-2:2024 Công nghệ thông tin - Các chỉ số hiệu quả chính của trung tâm dữ liệu - Phần 2: Hiệu suất sử dụng điện (PUE)

water.title: Mandatory data centre standard omits water
water.text: Circular 42/2025 sets the mandatory design standards for data centres. It sets no limit on water use, cooling efficiency or PUE.

sources.title: Thông tư 42/2025/TT-BKHCN: Tiêu chuẩn kỹ thuật cho trung tâm dữ liệu từ 2026

water.title: New building energy code excludes data centres
water.text: QCVN 04-3:2026/BXD sets energy efficiency rules, including chiller and air conditioning efficiency, for civil buildings of 2,500 square metres or more. Its listed building types are offices, hotels, hospitals, schools, malls and apartments. Data centres are absent from the list.

sources.title: QCVN 04-3:2026/BXD Công trình dân dụng - Sử dụng năng lượng hiệu quả

watching.title: Possible amendment of Circular 60
watching.text: EVN Ho Chi Minh City has asked the power ministry to amend Circular 60 to set how mixed use sites split their tariff. The ministry's Electricity Department said it is reviewing the rules and asked the parties to agree in the meantime.

sources.title: Trung tâm dữ liệu tính theo giá điện kinh doanh hay sản xuất?
Ministry urges production electricity tariffs for data centres

watching.title: Science ministry presses for production tariff
watching.text: The Ministry of Science and Technology sent its third letter to the power ministry on 15 September 2026. It asked that EVN apply the production rate to data centres in every region.

sources.title: EVN áp điện giá cao cho trung tâm dữ liệu: Bộ KH&CN gửi văn bản lần thứ 3 sang Bộ Công Thương

watching.title: Data centre power plan past its deadline
watching.text: The power supply plan for data centres under Resolution 262 was due in September 2026. No published plan was found by 3 October 2026.

sources.title: Điện cho trung tâm dữ liệu lỡ hạn 15/8, dời mốc hoàn thành sang tháng 9

watching.title: Draft 25 year tax break for strategic tech
watching.text: The Ministry of Finance has proposed amending Decree 320/2025 to give strategic technology enterprises 10% corporate tax for 25 years. The draft does not name data centres.

sources.title: Đề xuất áp thuế 10% suốt 25 năm cho doanh nghiệp công nghệ chiến lược

watching.title: Telecom Law amended again
watching.text: The National Assembly passed Law 20/2026/QH16 on 24 August 2026. It amends four laws including the Telecommunications Law and shifts toward checks after market entry. Its effect on data centre registration is not yet clear.

sources.title: Luật sửa đổi 4 luật về công nghệ, viễn thông: Đổi mới quản lý theo hướng tăng hậu kiểm, đẩy mạnh phân cấp, phân quyền

not_found: Could not confirm that EVN requires data centre operators to build their own 110kV substations.
The MOIT tariff letter is Dispatch 2818 dated 22 April 2026, reported in early May; no separate May 2026 letter was found.
Lead superseded. Decree 53/2022 was replaced by Decree 333/2026 from 19 August 2026.
Could not confirm whether MOIT delivered the Resolution 262 data centre power plan in September 2026.
Could not confirm the effective date of Law 20/2026/QH16.
No binding water use, water permit or cooling rule specific to data centres was found.

authorities.name: Government of Vietnam (Prime Minister and Cabinet)
match: Government; Ministry of Industry and Trade
Government; Ministry of Industry and Trade; EVN
Government; Ministry of Science and Technology
authorities.role: Issues the decrees that set data centre registration, direct power purchase and cybersecurity rules. Resolution 262/NQ-CP of 5 September 2026 ordered a power supply plan for data centres and high performance computing to 2030. The plan was due in September 2026 and had not been published by 3 October 2026.

authorities.name: Ministry of Industry and Trade (MOIT)
match: Government; Ministry of Industry and Trade
Government; Ministry of Industry and Trade; EVN
authorities.role: Sets power tariffs, direct power purchase rules and the national power plan. Circular 60/2025 put data centres on the business tariff. Dispatch 2818 of 22 April 2026 told EVN to bill technical systems at the cheaper production rate, but the State Audit Office says the dispatch has no legal force.

authorities.name: Vietnam Electricity (EVN) and its power corporations
match: State Audit Office; EVN Ho Chi Minh City
Government; Ministry of Industry and Trade; EVN
authorities.role: The state utility connects and bills every site through regional power corporations. In September 2026 EVN Ho Chi Minh City billed Viettel and CMC at the business rate. It threatened supply cuts over 11.35 billion dong in back charges.

authorities.name: Provincial People's Committees
authorities.role: Lease land and issue construction permits outside industrial zones and high-tech parks. Since Decree 133/2025 they also issue the telecom registration certificate a data centre needs before it sells services. In April 2026 the Da Nang People's Committee leased 10,000 square metres in the Da Nang Hi-Tech Park for the AIDC DECENTER data centre.

authorities.name: Management boards of high-tech parks and industrial zones
authorities.role: Approve investment policy and investors for projects inside their zones. They also oversee land allocation and issue construction permits there. The Da Nang Hi-Tech Park and Industrial Zones board approved the AIDC DECENTER project and its investor on 14 August 2025, with US$20 million in phase one.

authorities.name: Ministry of Science and Technology (MST)
match: Government; Ministry of Science and Technology
Bộ Khoa học và Công nghệ
authorities.role: The telecom regulator for data centres since it absorbed the former information ministry. Circular 42/2025 makes TCVN 9250, TIA 942 or Uptime tier standards mandatory from 1 February 2026, with self-declared conformity. On 15 September 2026 it sent its third letter asking for the production power tariff for data centres.

authorities.name: Ministry of Public Security (MPS)
match: National Assembly; Ministry of Public Security
authorities.role: Enforces the data localisation, personal data and data transfer rules. It receives transfer impact assessments and runs the National Data Centre. Decree 333/2026 of 19 August 2026 requires covered providers to store Vietnamese users' data in Vietnam.

authorities.name: Ministry of Finance and provincial Departments of Finance
authorities.role: Provincial Departments of Finance issue the investment registration certificate and the enterprise registration certificate. The ministry writes the corporate tax incentive rules. In September 2026 it proposed a 10% tax rate for 25 years for strategic technology firms, and the draft does not name data centres.

VN.authorities_note: Ranked by how much each body decides whether a project gets built in Vietnam today.
authorities_also: The National Assembly passes the telecom, investment, data, cybersecurity and tax laws, and amended the Telecommunications Law again on 24 August 2026.
The State Audit Office told EVN Ho Chi Minh City in 2026 to keep data centres on the business tariff.
The Ministry of Construction sets building codes, and its 2026 building energy code QCVN 04-3:2026 leaves out data centres.
The State Bank of Vietnam receives risk assessment reports when banks outsource systems or customer data to data centre providers.

PH.summary: The Philippines has no single data centre law, so projects rely on general investment, power and privacy rules. Data centres sit in the top tier of the 2026 Strategic Investment Priority Plan, and a July 2026 executive order now requires secret government data to stay in the country. Power remains the main constraint, after Luzon grid red alerts and rotating outages in May 2026.

approvals.title: Data transmission no longer needs a franchise
approvals.text: The Konektadong Pinoy Act (Republic Act 12234) lets data transmission providers build and run networks without a franchise from Congress. They register with the National Telecommunications Commission instead. The law does not name data centres, so its reach over pure data centre operators is unclear.

sources.title: Republic Act No. 12234
Implementing Rules and Regulations of the law removing congressional franchise requirement in the data transmission industry takes effect

approvals.title: Konektadong Pinoy rules are in force
approvals.text: DICT and six other agencies signed the implementing rules for the Konektadong Pinoy Act. The rules took effect after posting in the Official Gazette on 1 December 2025. Providers must hold an international cybersecurity certification within two years under the law.

sources.title: 'Konektadong Pinoy' IRR signed
Implementing Rules and Regulations of the law removing congressional franchise requirement in the data transmission industry takes effect

approvals.title: Green lane speeds permits for strategic projects
approvals.text: Executive Order 18 of 2023 created green lanes at the Board of Investments (BOI). A green lane certificate fast tracks permits and licences from national agencies and local governments for strategic investments.

sources.title: Executive Order No. 18, s. 2023

approvals.title: Converge Angeles gets green lane status
approvals.text: The BOI granted green lane status to the Converge ICT data centre in Angeles City, Pampanga, on 27 August 2026. The site cost nearly PHP 5 billion and started at 3 MW with room to grow to 36 MW.

sources.title: Converge secures faster permit processing for Angeles data center
Converge data center gets 'green lane' tag

approvals.title: Foreign ownership caps narrowed in 2022
approvals.text: The 2022 amendment to the Public Service Act (Republic Act 11659) limits the 40% foreign ownership cap to a short list of public utilities such as power distribution, transmission and water pipelines. Data centres are absent from that list. Foreign control of critical infrastructure above 50% needs reciprocity from the investor's home country.

sources.title: Philippines: President approves law removing foreign equity restrictions on public service companies

approvals.title: Metro Manila IT park moratorium lifted
approvals.text: The government exempted new IT parks in Metro Manila from a moratorium on new economic zones. This lets the Philippine Economic Zone Authority (PEZA) again accept IT park applications in the capital, and five parks applied soon after.

sources.title: PEZA lauds lifting of IT center moratorium in NCR
Five IT parks seek PEZA accreditation

power.title: Open access threshold cut to 100 kW
power.text: Since 26 June 2026, users with demand of at least 100 kW can buy power from a licensed retail supplier under Retail Competition and Open Access (RCOA). The threshold was 500 kW before. Smaller users can pool demand to qualify under the Retail Aggregation Program.

sources.title: ERC lowers retail choice threshold to 100 kW
DOE welcomes expanded consumer choice in electricity as contestability threshold drops to 100 kW

power.title: Green energy option opened to 50 kW
power.text: The Department of Energy (DOE) cut the Green Energy Option Program threshold from 100 kW to 50 kW. The program lets users contract renewable power directly from a supplier. Users in the same franchise area can now pool demand with no group size limit.

sources.title: DOE opens direct green energy contracting to more consumers

power.title: Meralco residential rate near PHP 14.74
power.text: Meralco's residential rate was PHP 14.7424 per kWh in September 2026. It was PHP 14.8261 in July and PHP 14.7833 in August. Meralco is the utility serving Metro Manila and nearby provinces.

sources.title: Lower Rates this September 2026
Higher Residential Rates this July 2026

power.title: Luzon grid hit red alert in May
power.text: The Luzon and Visayas grids went on red alert on 14 May 2026 after two 500 kV lines tripped. Luzon was short 413 MW, and Meralco cut power to over 200,000 customers for about three hours.

sources.title: Brownouts return as Luzon, Visayas grids hit red alert; here's what the terms mean

power.title: Meralco franchise renewed for 25 years
power.text: President Marcos signed a fresh 25 year franchise for Meralco on 11 April 2025. Areas outside Meralco use other utilities. Clark Electric is the sole distributor in the Clark Special Economic Zone in Pampanga and Tarlac.

sources.title: Marcos extends Meralco franchise for 25 years
How A Power Distributor Is Staying Ahead Of Clark’s Growth Spurt

power.title: No data centre power rule yet
power.text: No published DOE or ERC rule targets data centres. The ERC had not studied data centre impact on the power sector as of January 2026. The DOE estimates 300 to 1,500 MW of extra peak demand from data centres, pending validation.

sources.title: Data centers raise concerns for energy-burdened households

incentives.title: CREATE MORE gives 100% extra power deduction
incentives.text: The CREATE MORE Act (Republic Act 12066) was approved on 8 November 2024. Registered firms under its enhanced deductions regime pay 20% corporate income tax. They can also deduct power costs for registered activities a second time in full.

sources.title: Republic Act No. 12066

incentives.title: Local taxes capped at 2% of gross income
incentives.text: Under CREATE MORE, local governments may charge registered firms a local tax of up to 2% of gross income. This replaces all other local taxes, fees and charges.

sources.title: Republic Act No. 12066

incentives.title: Data centres in top investment tier
incentives.text: The 2026 Strategic Investment Priority Plan places data centre facilities in Tier III, its highest tier, with cybersecurity and artificial intelligence. The President approved it through Memorandum Order 47, signed on 21 May 2026.

sources.title: President Marcos approves 2026 Strategic Investment Priority Plan

incentives.title: VAT zero rating needs 70% exports
incentives.text: Registered firms get VAT exemption on imports and zero rated local purchases only if export sales reach at least 70% of output. Data centres serving mainly local clients may not meet this test.

sources.title: Republic Act No. 12066

data.title: Privacy law allows transfers abroad
data.text: The Data Privacy Act of 2012 does not require personal data to stay in the country. A company that sends data abroad for processing stays responsible for it. It must use contracts or other means to give comparable protection.

sources.title: Republic Act 10173 - Data Privacy Act of 2012

data.title: Model transfer clauses are voluntary
data.text: The National Privacy Commission (NPC) issued model contract clauses for cross border transfers in May 2024. Use is voluntary, and the NPC will not review contracts for conformity.

sources.title: Model Contractual Clauses for Cross-Border Transfers of Personal Data

data.title: EO 119 keeps secret government data onshore
data.text: Executive Order 119, signed in mid July 2026, requires Top Secret and Secret government data to stay in Philippine territory. Confidential data generally stays local unless a joint committee approves offshore processing. Lower classes may use secure cloud platforms, and the order does not cover private sector data.
data.authority: Office of the President, DICT, NSC

sources.title: New EO sets gov’t data residency rules, requires local storage of sensitive data
Marcos orders government data overhaul

data.title: Agencies get three years to comply
data.text: Agencies must finish data inventories in year one and fully comply for Top Secret and Secret data by year two. All government data must comply by year three.

sources.title: New EO sets gov’t data residency rules, requires local storage of sensitive data

data.title: Cloud First Policy guides agency hosting
data.text: DICT's Cloud First Policy pushes government agencies to use cloud services. A 2020 amendment set four classes of government data and stated that Philippine law applies to government data with local links.

sources.title: DICT amends cloud-first policy

data.title: Bank outsourcing rules cover cloud risk
data.text: Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) Circular 1137 of 2022 makes banks classify outsourcing as material or non material. Banks stay responsible for checking providers' security and must assess data access risks from provider staff.

sources.title: Rules on outsourcing tightened

water.title: Water use needs an NWRB permit
water.text: Under the Water Code of 1976, no one may draw water without a water permit. The National Water Resources Board (NWRB) now issues these permits, including for groundwater and industrial use.

water.title: Metro Manila water allocation cut
water.text: The NWRB cut Angat Dam water for Metro Manila from 50 to 53 cubic metres per second to 44 for October 2026. It acted ahead of a strong El Niño. Angat supplies most of the capital's water.

sources.title: Metro Manila water allocation cut as Super El Niño looms
Metro Manila water allocation from Angat down

water.title: No data centre water rule yet
water.text: No national rule sets water or cooling limits for data centres. Engineering firm Black & Veatch said in May 2026 that operators need certainty on both power and water supply.

sources.title: ‘Power infrastructure not yet ready for data center boom’

watching.title: EO 119 guidelines due within 120 days
watching.text: A joint committee led by DICT and the National Security Council must issue implementing guidelines within 120 days of the order taking effect. That points to around November 2026.

sources.title: President Marcos Signs EO 119, Unlocking Digital Infrastructure Growth and Strengthening Philippine Data Security

watching.title: DOE data centre energisation policy pending
watching.text: Energy Secretary Sharon Garin said the DOE would release a data centre energisation policy in 2026. No published policy was found as of 3 October 2026.

sources.title: ‘Power infrastructure not yet ready for data center boom’

watching.title: Bill to make green lanes law
watching.text: House Bill 2781, filed on 31 July 2025, would turn the green lane scheme into law. It sets 3, 7 and 20 working day deadlines and automatic approval if agencies miss them.

sources.title: Green Lanes for Strategic Investments Act

watching.title: ERC roadmap for wider retail choice
watching.text: The ERC plans to publish a roadmap for phased expansion of retail choice programs. The stated end goal is to let households choose their supplier.

sources.title: RCOA threshold reduced to 100 kW

watching.title: DICT targets 18 GW over a decade
watching.text: DICT Secretary Henry Aguda set a goal of 18 GW of data centre capacity over ten years, with 1.5 GW by end 2027. The government is also studying turning the Bataan Nuclear Power Plant into a data centre site.

sources.title: DICT outlines massive 18GW data center expansion to lead ASEAN

watching.title: Push for a private data residency law
watching.text: Investment bankers have urged a broad data residency law covering private data. They say it would support data centre demand and future listings.

sources.title: As data centers multiply, localization pushed

The lead residential rate of PHP 14.83 per kWh was Meralco's July 2026 rate and is superseded by PHP 14.7424 in September 2026.
No source confirms Converge Angeles was the first data centre to receive a green lane certificate; a separate BOI notice on a 36 MW data centre green lane could not be read.
No DICT registration or licence specific to data centre operators was found.
No bill in the 20th Congress specifically regulating data centres was found.
No DOE or ERC circular aimed at data centres has been published as of 3 October 2026.
No national water or cooling efficiency rule for data centres was found.
No BSP rule mandating onshore storage of bank data was found.
Exact EO 119 signing date is reported as 13 July and 16 July 2026 by different sources.

authorities.name: Board of Investments (BOI)
authorities.role: Registers data centre projects for incentives. The 2026 Strategic Investment Priority Plan puts them in Tier III, the highest tier. It also issues green lane certificates that fast-track national and local permits. On 27 August 2026 it gave green lane status to Converge ICT's Angeles City data centre.

authorities.name: Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT)
match: Office of the President, DICT, NSC
authorities.role: Leads digital infrastructure policy. In February 2026 it set a goal of 18 GW of data centre capacity in ten years, with 1.5 GW by end 2027. It co-leads the committee writing the guidelines for the Executive Order 119 data residency rules, due around November 2026.

authorities.name: Department of Energy (DOE)
authorities.role: Sets energy policy and runs the Green Energy Option Program, now open to users of 50 kW and up. Energy Secretary Sharon Garin said the DOE would release a data centre energisation policy in 2026. None was published by 3 October 2026.

authorities.name: Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC)
authorities.role: Approves utility rates and runs retail competition. Since 26 June 2026, users of 100 kW or more can buy from a licensed retail supplier. It had not studied data centre impact on the power sector as of January 2026.

authorities.name: National Grid Corporation of the Philippines (NGCP)
match: National Grid Corporation of the Philippines
authorities.role: Runs the national transmission grid. Large sites depend on its lines and substations. The Luzon and Visayas grids went on red alert on 14 May 2026 after two 500 kV lines tripped, leaving Luzon 413 MW short.

authorities.name: Meralco and other distribution utilities
authorities.role: Connect and supply sites in their franchise areas. Meralco serves Metro Manila and nearby provinces and got a fresh 25-year franchise on 11 April 2025. Clark Electric is the sole distributor in the Clark Special Economic Zone.

authorities.name: Philippine Economic Zone Authority (PEZA)
authorities.role: Registers economic zones, IT parks and the firms located in them for incentives. In July 2026 the government exempted new Metro Manila IT parks from the moratorium on new zones. Five parks applied to PEZA soon after.

authorities.name: Fiscal Incentives Review Board (FIRB)
authorities.role: Decides tax incentives for projects above PHP 15 billion of investment capital. Investment promotion agencies such as the BOI and PEZA decide smaller ones. The board set this threshold in Resolution 003-24 on 2 February 2024.

authorities.name: National Water Resources Board (NWRB)
authorities.role: Issues the water permit needed to draw groundwater or surface water. For October 2026 it cut Angat Dam water for Metro Manila to 44 cubic metres per second, ahead of a strong El Niño.

authorities.name: Local government units
authorities.role: Cities and municipalities issue local permits and clearances. Green lane certificates under Executive Order 18 require them to fast-track permits for strategic projects. Under CREATE MORE they may charge registered firms up to 2% of gross income in place of other local taxes.

PH.authorities_note: Ranked by how much each body decides whether a project gets built in the Philippines today.
authorities_also: The National Privacy Commission (NPC) enforces the Data Privacy Act, which allows transfers abroad with comparable protection.
The National Security Council (NSC) co-leads with DICT the committee that sets which government data must stay onshore under Executive Order 119.
The Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA) said on 7 August 2026 that its Pax Silica site in New Clark City will not host hyperscale data centres.
The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) sets outsourcing rules that banks apply when they use cloud and data centre providers.

IN.summary: India has no national data centre policy in force, so each state sets its own terms on land, power and incentives. Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Karnataka all issued new or expanded data centre policies in 2026, and most now tie support to renewable power or efficiency targets. The largest national change is the data protection regime, which brings most obligations and the cross-border transfer rules into force on 13 May 2027.

approvals.title: National data centre policy still a draft
approvals.text: India has no notified national data centre policy. MeitY (the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology) revived its unreleased 2020 draft in 2025, and the revised draft proposes a tax holiday of up to 20 years, a single-window clearance to replace more than 30 permissions, and four data centre economic zones. We found no final notified version as of October 2026.
approvals.authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)

sources.title: India revives national datacentre policy amid AI push
Govt proposes tax exemption of up to 20 years for data centre developers

approvals.title: Infrastructure status for data centres
approvals.text: Data centres with at least 5 MW of IT load are listed as infrastructure on the national harmonised master list. Listed sectors can access infrastructure lending on easier terms.
approvals.authority: Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance

sources.title: Updated Harmonized Master List of Infrastructure Sub-sectors

approvals.title: Uttar Pradesh Data Centre Policy 2026
approvals.text: The Uttar Pradesh cabinet approved a new data centre policy on 7 July 2026. It targets 2 GW of new capacity and Rs 2 lakh crore of investment, with extra support for GPU and Tier III or Tier IV facilities. Land subsidy is 50% in Bundelkhand and Purvanchal and 25% elsewhere, although all seven projects under the 2021 policy sit in Noida or Greater Noida.

sources.title: Uttar Pradesh: Cabinet approves data center policy 2026; Targets Rs 2 lakh crore investment and 50,000 Jobs
Uttar Pradesh's Data Centre Policy Gets Almost Everything Right—One Clause Is The Exception

approvals.title: Karnataka Sustainable Data Centre Policy 2026 to 2031
approvals.text: Karnataka's cabinet approved a five-year data centre policy in September 2026 with a budget of Rs 1,300.45 crore and a goal of 1 GW of IT load by 2031. Karnataka Udyoga Mitra is the single-window clearance agency for approvals. Three parks are planned at Hoskote, Mangaluru and Mysuru.
approvals.authority: Government of Karnataka, Department of Electronics, IT, Biotechnology and Science and Technology

sources.title: Karnataka Approves Sustainable Data Centre Policy 2026–2031
Karnataka's new data centre policy puts water, energy in focus: What does it say?

approvals.title: Gujarat Data Centre Policy 2026 to 2029
approvals.text: Gujarat launched its first dedicated data centre policy in July 2026, valid to 2029, with a 7.5 GW capacity goal. Projects need at least 150 MW of approved IT load to qualify. Facilities must source at least 51% of their electricity from renewable sources.

sources.title: Gujarat Launches Ambitious Data Centre Policy; Eyes More Than ₹6 Lakh cr Investment in First Phase
Gujarat Unveils Data Centre Policy To Build 7.5 GW Capacity And Attract Rs 6 Lakh Crore Investment

approvals.title: Maharashtra green data centre parks go statewide
approvals.text: Maharashtra expanded its Green Integrated Data Centre Parks policy in June 2026 from 3 parks in the Mumbai region to 20 parks across the state. The share of green power required for core operations fell from 100% to 51%.

sources.title: Maharashtra Expands Green Data Centre Policy: Investor Impact
Indian state gov't approves large scale sustainable data center project

approvals.title: Andhra Pradesh approves projects case by case
approvals.text: Andhra Pradesh approves large data centres one by one through government orders under its Data Center Policy 4.0 for 2024 to 2029. In August 2026 it cleared four projects worth Rs 2.83 lakh crore, each with its own mix of land, power and tax concessions.
approvals.authority: Government of Andhra Pradesh, IT, Electronics and Communications Department

sources.title: Andhra Pradesh clears four data centres worth Rs 2.83 lakh crore

approvals.title: Tamil Nadu policy period has ended
approvals.text: Tamil Nadu's Data Centre Policy 2021 applied from 1 April 2021 to 31 March 2026. We found no successor policy, so the terms for new projects are unclear.

sources.title: TN government launches Data Centre policy; plans to provide incentives of ₹500 crore

approvals.title: MIDC data centre parks at Taloja and Khalapur
approvals.text: MIDC set aside 100 hectares at Taloja in Navi Mumbai and 500 hectares at Khalapur in Raigad for data centre parks in September 2019. MIDC said it would manage the parks and prepare a policy to convert land for data centre use.

sources.title: Maharashtra To Provide Additional Land For Data Centre Infrastructure

approvals.title: Tamil Nadu fast track for large projects
approvals.text: An amendment to the Tamil Nadu Business Facilitation Act, notified in September 2026, sets up the Tamil Nadu Investment Promotion Authority under the Chief Secretary. It monitors projects of Rs 200 crore or more or with at least 5,000 jobs, so most large data centres qualify. Departments must give approvals within set time limits. Press reports cite 21 days, but the notified text was not seen.
approvals.authority: Government of Tamil Nadu; Tamil Nadu Investment Promotion Authority

sources.title: 21-day approval for investment projects in TN

power.title: Uttar Pradesh bills data centres as industry
power.text: Uttar Pradesh moved data centres into the HV-2 large and heavy power tariff, the industrial class, after a state notification of 4 October 2024. Before that they paid the commercial rate. No other state has a tariff written for data centres that we could confirm.

sources.title: ARR and Tariff of NIDP for FY 2026-27, APR of FY 2025-26 and True-up of FY 2024-25

power.title: Greater Noida data centre park tariff
power.text: NIDP Developers runs its own power distribution licence inside a Greater Noida data centre park. For the 2026 to 2027 year its HV-2 rate is Rs 270 per kVA per month of contract demand plus Rs 6.95 per kVAh of energy. A kVAh is a billing unit close to a kWh.

sources.title: ARR and Tariff of NIDP for FY 2026-27, APR of FY 2025-26 and True-up of FY 2024-25

power.title: UPPCL HV-2 industrial rates for 2026 to 2027
power.text: State utility customers in the urban HV-2 class pay a demand charge of Rs 270 to 300 per kVA per month. Energy costs Rs 7.10 per kVAh at up to 11 kV, falling to Rs 6.10 above 132 kV. Time of day rates add or cut 15% in peak and off-peak hours.

sources.title: ARR and Tariff of State Discoms for FY 2026-27, APR of FY 2025-26 and True-up of FY 2024-25

power.title: Green Energy Open Access Rules 2022
power.text: Consumers with 100 kW or more can buy renewable power directly from generators through open access, meaning use of the grid to buy from someone other than the local utility. Applications must be decided within 15 days or are deemed approved. Utilities must bank surplus green power, and cross-subsidy surcharges are capped.

sources.title: Ministry of Power notifies the Green Energy Open Access Rules

power.title: Uttar Pradesh transmission charge waiver
power.text: Under the Uttar Pradesh Data Centre Policy 2021, data centre parks get a 50% waiver on intra-state wheeling and transmission charges for 25 years. The state transmission company began applying the waiver to bills from April 2025.
power.authority: Government of Uttar Pradesh; UP Power Transmission Corporation

sources.title: ARR and Tariff of NIDP for FY 2026-27, APR of FY 2025-26 and True-up of FY 2024-25

power.title: Maharashtra lets data centres make green power
power.text: A Maharashtra energy department order of 6 October 2025 lets data centre parks build captive solar, wind and hydro supply and distribute it within designated zones. Operators need a parallel distribution licence from MERC, the state electricity regulator.
power.authority: Government of Maharashtra, Energy Department; Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission (MERC)

sources.title: Maharashtra Allows Data Centres to Generate Green Power

power.title: Tamil Nadu dual grid for large sites
power.text: Tamil Nadu's 2021 policy offered a dual grid connection, meaning two independent feeders, to data centres with 50 MW or more of sanctioned load. It also offered reduced cross-subsidy surcharges on wind and solar power.

sources.title: TN government launches Data Centre policy; plans to provide incentives of ₹500 crore

power.title: Telangana renewable open access limit
power.text: Telangana's Data Centres Policy of 2016 lets data centres buy renewable power through open access for up to one third of their needs. They must pay the utility charges set by the state regulator.

sources.title: Hyderabad well-placed for data centres

power.title: MSEDCL bills data centres as industry
power.text: MERC's multi-year tariff order for MSEDCL of 28 March 2025 put data centres in the industrial category from 1 April 2025. Data centres that buy 100% green power through open access or a green tariff get a 10% discount on wheeling charges. The tariff levels were later revised. MERC's final review order of 25 March 2026 applies revised rates from 1 July 2025. We did not confirm that the review kept the data centre terms unchanged.

sources.title: Mahavitaran Consumers To Pay Less: MERC Orders Major Power Tariff Reduction
MERC issues final order on MSEDCL tariff review after court intervention

incentives.title: Federal tax holiday for foreign cloud
incentives.text: Foreign cloud companies pay no Indian tax on income from services sold outside India through data centres in India, up to the 2046 to 2047 tax year. The data centre must be run by an Indian company and notified by MeitY, and Indian customers must buy through an Indian reseller. Indian data centres serving a related foreign company can use a fixed 15% margin on costs for tax.

sources.title: Budget 2026–27 Sets the Stage for India as a Global Hub for Cloud and AI Infrastructure
Indian Budget 2026-27: Tax Incentives for Data Centres

incentives.title: Gujarat power subsidy and duty waivers
incentives.text: Gujarat pays a power tariff subsidy of Rs 1 per unit for 20 years and reimburses electricity duty for 20 years. Stamp duty and registration fees are fully waived. Total support is capped at 75% of eligible fixed capital investment.

sources.title: Gujarat Launches Ambitious Data Centre Policy; Eyes More Than ₹6 Lakh cr Investment in First Phase

incentives.title: Maharashtra power and capital support
incentives.text: Maharashtra parks get a power tariff concession of Rs 1 per unit for 10 years at Rs 30,000 crore of investment, or 20 years at Rs 60,000 crore or more. The larger projects can also get an industrial incentive of up to 75% and a 4% interest subsidy on term loans, capped at Rs 25 crore a year for 10 years.

sources.title: Maharashtra Expands Green Data Centre Policy: Investor Impact

incentives.title: Uttar Pradesh 2021 policy incentives
incentives.text: Under the 2021 policy, data centre units get a capital subsidy of 7% of eligible fixed capital, capped at Rs 20 crore. They also get a full stamp duty waiver on the first land deal and a 10-year electricity duty exemption. The detailed figures in the 2026 policy were not public in sources we found.

sources.title: Uttar Pradesh Data Centre Policy, 2021: Key features, incentives, eligibility and implementation

incentives.title: Andhra Pradesh package for Google Vizag
incentives.text: Andhra Pradesh gave Google a 25% land price discount, a stamp duty waiver and an electricity duty exemption for its Visakhapatnam site. The package also includes Rs 1 off the industrial power tariff and State GST refunds during construction capped at Rs 2,245 crore.

sources.title: Inside the subsidies for Google's Vizag data centre amid Andhra-Karnataka spar

incentives.title: IndiaAI Mission subsidised GPU compute
incentives.text: The IndiaAI Mission has onboarded 38,000 GPUs from private providers and is adding 20,000 more. Users pay a subsidised rate of Rs 65 per GPU hour. The mission has a five-year budget of Rs 10,371.92 crore approved in March 2024.

sources.title: India to Add 20,000 GPUs as AI Mission 2.0 Expands Compute and Chip Push

incentives.title: PLI 2.0 covers server manufacturing
incentives.text: The production linked incentive scheme for IT hardware pays makers of laptops, PCs and servers in India. It has an outlay of Rs 17,000 crore over six years.

sources.title: Cabinet approves PLI Scheme 2.0 for IT Hardware with Rs 17,000 cr budget

data.title: DPDP Rules 2025 phased in
data.text: The Digital Personal Data Protection Rules were notified in November 2025 with an 18-month phase-in. Consent manager rules start on 13 November 2026. Most duties on data fiduciaries, meaning firms that decide how personal data is used, start on 13 May 2027.

sources.title: DPDP Rules, 2025 Notified
Cross-Border Data Transfers Under India's DPDP Act: Rules, Restrictions And Compliance Roadmap For 2027

data.title: Cross-border transfers use a negative list
data.text: Personal data may leave India unless the government restricts a named country. No restricted list has been notified. The transfer rules start on 13 May 2027, and significant data fiduciaries may face local storage duties for some data types.

sources.title: Cross-Border Data Transfers Under India's DPDP Act: Rules, Restrictions And Compliance Roadmap For 2027

data.title: RBI payment data stays in India
data.text: Since a 2018 RBI directive, all payment system data must be stored only in India. Data processed abroad must be deleted there and returned to India within one business day or 24 hours.

sources.title: RBI issues clarifications on data localisation circular

data.title: SEBI cloud framework requires India storage
data.text: SEBI's 2023 cloud framework requires regulated securities firms to store and process data in the cloud within India. It applies to brokers, exchanges and other market entities.
data.authority: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)

sources.title: India's stock market regulator mandates securities sector to store data locally

data.title: CERT-In logs kept in India
data.text: CERT-In, the national cyber security agency, requires covered entities to keep logs of all ICT systems for 180 days within India. Data centre, cloud and virtual server providers must keep customer records for five years. Cyber incidents must be reported within six hours.

sources.title: Internet Impact Brief: India CERT-In Cybersecurity Directions 2022

water.title: No national water rule for data centres
water.text: India has no water rule written for data centres. Data centre buildings over 20,000 square metres need prior environmental clearance, which reviews freshwater supply, water balance and reuse. Groundwater use falls under Ministry of Jal Shakti extraction guidelines.
water.authority: State Environment Impact Assessment Authorities; Ministry of Jal Shakti

sources.title: India Strengthens Water Management Rules for AI Data Centres

water.title: Karnataka pays for water efficiency
water.text: Karnataka reimburses 100% of treated water charges up to Rs 8 lakh a year for five years. Units with water usage effectiveness of 0.7 to 1.3 litres per kWh can get up to Rs 30 lakh a year for two years. The planned Hoskote park has access to 60 million litres a day of treated wastewater.

sources.title: Karnataka's new data centre policy puts water, energy in focus: What does it say?

water.title: Gujarat funds desalination for data centres
water.text: Gujarat offers up to Rs 2 crore per million litres a day of captive desalination capacity built for data centres.

sources.title: Gujarat Launches Ambitious Data Centre Policy; Eyes More Than ₹6 Lakh cr Investment in First Phase

water.title: Treated wastewater for cooling encouraged
water.text: Bureau of Energy Efficiency district cooling guidelines from 2023 encourage treated wastewater in place of freshwater for cooling towers. The guidelines are voluntary.

sources.title: India Strengthens Water Management Rules for AI Data Centres

watching.title: DPDP consent manager phase
watching.text: Consent manager rules under the DPDP Rules start on 13 November 2026. Consent managers are registered platforms that let people give and withdraw consent across services.

sources.title: Cross-Border Data Transfers Under India's DPDP Act: Rules, Restrictions And Compliance Roadmap For 2027

watching.title: DPDP full obligations and transfer rules
watching.text: Most DPDP duties and the cross-border transfer rules start on 13 May 2027. Any restricted country list would be notified by the central government.

sources.title: Cross-Border Data Transfers Under India's DPDP Act: Rules, Restrictions And Compliance Roadmap For 2027

watching.title: Shorter DPDP timeline for large firms
watching.text: In January 2026 MeitY proposed cutting the compliance period for significant data fiduciaries from 18 months to 12 months. It also proposed starting cross-border restrictions at once. As of September 2026 no amendment had been notified.

sources.title: Meity may cut compliance timeline for key DPDP rules to 12 months
Cross-Border Data Transfers Under India's DPDP Act: Rules, Restrictions And Compliance Roadmap For 2027

watching.title: Final national data centre policy
watching.text: MeitY expected to finalise the national data centre policy in late 2025. It has not been released. The draft includes tax holidays, single-window clearance and data centre economic zones.

sources.title: India revives national datacentre policy amid AI push

watching.title: Adani power licence for Noida data centre park
watching.text: UPERC admitted a petition in August 2026 from an Adani Energy Solutions unit for a parallel distribution licence at a Noida Sector 62 data centre park. The applicant must publish notices and take objections for 30 days before a decision.

sources.title: UPERC Advances Adani Energy Solutions' Parallel Power Distribution License Application For Noida Data Centre Park
Uttar Pradesh Regulator Admits Data Center Power Distribution License Plea

watching.title: CEA draft grid connection standards
watching.text: The Central Electricity Authority issued draft technical standards for grid connection in July 2026. They would cover bulk consumers connected at 33 kV and above, which includes large data centres.

sources.title: CEA issues Draft CEA (Technical Standards for Connectivity to the Grid) Regulations, 2026

watching.title: West Bengal policy term ending
watching.text: West Bengal's Data Centre Policy was notified on 6 September 2021 for five years. It offers a full stamp duty waiver and a five-year electricity duty waiver. We found no renewal or successor policy.

sources.title: West Bengal Data Centre Policy, 2021

authorities.name: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
match: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
authorities.role: Owns the national data centre policy, which is still an unreleased draft. Under the Finance Act 2026 it notifies which Indian-run data centres qualify for the foreign cloud tax holiday to 2047. It also runs the DPDP data protection rules.

authorities.name: Ministry of Power
authorities.role: Sets national power rules, including the 2022 green energy open access rules for users of 100 kW or more. In July 2026 it began a countrywide exercise with the CEA, utilities and developers to map data centre power demand and plan the grid. Internal estimates put demand at 26 GW by 2032.

authorities.name: Central Electricity Authority (CEA)
authorities.role: Sets technical standards for the grid. In July 2026 it issued draft grid connection standards. They would cover bulk consumers connected at 33 kV and above, which includes large data centres.

authorities.name: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and State Environment Impact Assessment Authorities (SEIAA)
match: State Environment Impact Assessment Authorities; Ministry of Jal Shakti
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
authorities.role: The ministry told Parliament on 6 August 2026 that AI data centres do not need environmental clearance as such. Large sites still need it as building projects, which a state authority grants. The Andhra Pradesh SEIAA cleared the Google-Adani Vizag site on 5 June 2026 on its built-up area, and that clearance is now challenged in the High Court.

authorities.name: Government of Maharashtra
match: Government of Maharashtra, Energy Department; Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission (MERC)
authorities.role: Sets the terms in India's largest data centre market. In June 2026 it widened its Green Integrated Data Centre Parks policy from 3 parks to 20 statewide and cut the green power share for core operations from 100% to 51%. An energy department order of 6 October 2025 lets parks build their own green supply.

authorities.name: Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission (MERC)
match: Government of Maharashtra, Energy Department; Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission (MERC)
authorities.role: Sets tariffs and grants distribution licences in Maharashtra. A data centre park that wants to distribute its own green power inside a designated zone needs a parallel distribution licence from MERC.

authorities.name: Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company (MSEDCL, Mahavitaran)
authorities.role: The state distribution company. It already supplies the Mumbai suburbs of Mulund and Bhandup. In June 2025 it asked MERC for a parallel licence across much of Mumbai and cited the data centre boom as a driver of demand.

authorities.name: Government of Uttar Pradesh (Department of IT and Electronics)
match: Government of Uttar Pradesh; UP Power Transmission Corporation
authorities.role: The state cabinet approved the Data Centre Policy 2026 on 7 July 2026, with a 2 GW target. A nodal agency under the IT department takes applications through the Nivesh Mitra single window. Projects over Rs 200 crore need cabinet approval on an empowered committee's recommendation.

authorities.name: Uttar Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission (UPERC)
authorities.role: Sets the industrial HV-2 tariff that data centres in the state pay, and grants distribution licences. In August 2026 it admitted an Adani Energy Solutions petition for a parallel distribution licence at a Noida Sector 62 data centre park.

authorities.name: Uttar Pradesh distribution and transmission companies (UPPCL, NIDP Developers and UPPTCL)
match: Government of Uttar Pradesh; UP Power Transmission Corporation
authorities.role: The state discoms under UPPCL supply most sites. NIDP Developers holds its own distribution licence inside a Greater Noida data centre park. The state transmission company began applying the 50% transmission charge waiver for data centre parks from April 2025.

authorities.name: Government of Tamil Nadu
authorities.role: Its Data Centre Policy 2021 ended on 31 March 2026, and no successor was found. At an investment event on 13 August 2026, data centres took Rs 26,417 crore of the commitments. They included a Rs 10,000 crore hyperscale site by Lighthouse Green Data Centre at Thoothukudi.

authorities.name: Tamil Nadu Investment Promotion Authority
authorities.role: A body chaired by the Chief Secretary to fast-track projects of Rs 200 crore or more or with at least 5,000 jobs. An amendment to the Tamil Nadu Business Facilitation Act was notified in September 2026 and sets time limits for approvals. Press reports give the body two different names.

authorities.name: Government of Andhra Pradesh (IT, Electronics and Communications Department)
match: Government of Andhra Pradesh, IT, Electronics and Communications Department
authorities.role: Approves large data centres one by one through government orders under Data Center Policy 4.0. Each order sets its own land, power and tax concessions. In August 2026 it cleared four projects worth Rs 2.83 lakh crore.

authorities.name: Government of Karnataka and Karnataka Udyoga Mitra
match: Government of Karnataka, Department of Electronics, IT, Biotechnology and Science and Technology
authorities.role: The cabinet approved the Sustainable Data Centre Policy 2026 to 2031 in September 2026, aiming for 1 GW of IT load. Karnataka Udyoga Mitra is the single window for clearances. Karnataka Innovation and Technology Services registers projects for incentives.

authorities.name: Government of Telangana
authorities.role: Its 2016 Data Centres Policy lets data centres buy renewable power through open access for up to one third of their needs. The state electricity regulator sets the charges they pay the discoms. No newer Telangana data centre policy was confirmed.

authorities.name: Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation (MIDC)
authorities.role: Allots industrial land in Maharashtra and runs data centre parks on it. In 2019 it set aside 100 hectares at Taloja and 500 hectares at Khalapur for data centre parks.

IN.authorities_note: Central bodies first, then the main data centre states. Within each group, ranked by how much each body decides whether a project gets built today.
authorities_also: The Department of Economic Affairs in the Ministry of Finance lists data centres of 5 MW or more as infrastructure, which opens cheaper infrastructure lending.
CERT-In requires data centre and cloud providers to keep logs in India for 180 days and customer records for five years.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) requires all payment system data to be stored only in India.
The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) requires regulated securities firms to store and process cloud data within India.
The Ministry of Jal Shakti sets the groundwater extraction rules that apply to data centres, which have no water rule written for them.
The Bureau of Energy Efficiency encourages treated wastewater for cooling through voluntary 2023 district cooling guidelines.
The Government of Gujarat launched a data centre policy in July 2026, valid to 2029, for projects of 150 MW or more with at least 51% renewable power.
The Government of West Bengal notified a five-year data centre policy on 6 September 2021, and no renewal was found.

AE.summary: The UAE has no single licence for data centres, so projects move through free zone, land and utility approvals in each emirate. The biggest rule in play is a US export rule from 10 July 2026 that lets G42 and Core42 receive advanced AI chips without a licence, but only until 6 April 2027 unless they become US companies. Power is cheaper in Abu Dhabi than Dubai, and Abu Dhabi is still designing a special tariff for data centres.

approvals.title: US eases chip exports to the UAE
approvals.text: On 10 July 2026 the US Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) moved the UAE into Country Group A, subgroup 5. This makes UAE buyers eligible for a licence exception called Strategic Trade Authorization. The UAE was also removed from two groups of countries of concern for chemical, biological and missile items.
approvals.authority: US Bureau of Industry and Security

sources.title: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
sources.publisher: Federal Register (US Bureau of Industry and Security)

approvals.title: Named UAE buyers can receive AI chips
approvals.text: The same rule created a list of approved end users in Supplement No. 8 to Part 740 of US export rules. It names UAE government bodies, G42 and Core42, and eight US companies including Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Oracle and OpenAI. Listed parties can receive advanced computing items without a separate export licence.
approvals.authority: US Bureau of Industry and Security

sources.title: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
sources.publisher: Federal Register (US Bureau of Industry and Security)

approvals.title: Abu Dhabi leases government land to developers
approvals.text: The Abu Dhabi Investment Office (ADIO) runs the Musataha programme, which gives companies long-term leases over government-owned land. Khazna used it in 2024 for a 30 MW data centre in Mafraq. ADIO said it had signed 132 such agreements since October 2021.

sources.title: Abu Dhabi Investment Office collaborates with Khazna to build advanced data centre under Musataha programme

approvals.title: Dubai free zone authority supplies land
approvals.text: The Dubai Integrated Economic Zones Authority (DIEZ) runs free zones including Dubai Silicon Oasis. In May 2026 it formed a joint venture with Volt UAE for a data centre campus there. DIEZ provides land and base infrastructure and Volt builds, finances and operates the site.

sources.title: Dubai authority partners with Volt for AI-ready data centre

approvals.title: Telecom licences renewed with resilience duties
approvals.text: The Telecommunications and Digital Government Regulatory Authority (TDRA) renewed the licences of e& and du from 9 August 2026 to 8 August 2046. The new licences add duties on network resilience, backup capacity and international connectivity. These two carriers supply most connectivity to UAE data centres.
approvals.authority: Telecommunications and Digital Government Regulatory Authority

sources.title: TDRA Board Renews Telecom Licences of Both Operators for Another 20 Years

power.title: Dubai industrial tariff tops out at 38 fils
power.text: DEWA charges industrial users AED 0.230 per kWh for the first 10,000 kWh each month and AED 0.380 above that. A large data centre pays almost all its power at the upper rate. The slabs come from a 2011 Dubai Executive Council resolution.

sources.title: Slab Tariff
Executive Council Resolution No. (16) of 2011 Approving the Electricity and Water Tariff in the Emirate of Dubai

power.title: Dubai adds a monthly fuel surcharge
power.text: DEWA adds a fuel surcharge that it resets each month. For October 2026 it is AED 0.060 per kWh. With 5% VAT the upper band costs about AED 0.462, or about US$0.126 per kWh.

sources.title: Slab Tariff

power.title: Abu Dhabi large industry pays 27 fils off-peak
power.text: In Abu Dhabi, industrial users above 1 MW pay 27 fils per kWh off-peak, about US$0.074. The peak rate is 36.6 fils from 10am to 10pm between 1 June and 30 September. Users of 1 MW or less pay a flat 28.6 fils.

sources.title: Business Rates And Tariffs 2025

power.title: Abu Dhabi designs a data centre tariff
power.text: The Abu Dhabi Department of Energy said in January 2026 that it is designing a dedicated electricity tariff for data centres. It wants prices that compete globally while covering the real cost of supply. Operators may be able to choose their energy mix, including renewables. No rates had been published by 3 October 2026.

sources.title: Abu Dhabi to Introduce Dedicated Power Tariff for AI Data Centres

power.title: National team reviews data centre energy use
power.text: The national team that reviews how data centres affect the energy sector met for the first time on 3 February 2025 at MoEI in Dubai. It will measure data centre power demand, list and classify every data centre and map current and planned sites. It must also draft a federal policy to regulate data centre operations. No policy had been published by October 2026.

sources.title: National Team for Reviewing the Impact of Data Centers on Energy Sector Holds First Meeting

power.title: EWEC and Masdar round-the-clock solar project
power.text: EWEC and Masdar are developing a 5.2 GW solar plant with 19 GWh of battery storage in Abu Dhabi to supply 1 GW of steady power for 24 hours. The project reached financial close on 13 July 2026 and should operate in 2027. Masdar named AI and data centres as drivers of demand. No offtake contract with a data centre has been announced.

sources.title: Masdar secures funding for $6.1bn round-the-clock clean energy project
Masdar hits financial close on 5.2GW/19GWh 'round-the-clock' solar-plus-storage project

power.title: TAQA plans AED 37 billion for data centre power
power.text: TAQA's CEO said on 29 May 2025 that investment to power Abu Dhabi's data centre industry will exceed AED 37 billion, about US$10 billion. TAQA is building a 1 GW gas turbine station and plans to spend AED 75 billion by 2030 to grow its generation capacity to 150 GW.

sources.title: Abu Dhabi's data centre industry power investments to exceed Dh37 bn: TAQA CEO

incentives.title: Corporate tax is 9% above AED 375,000
incentives.text: Federal corporate tax is 0% on taxable income up to AED 375,000 and 9% above it. It applies to financial years starting on or after 1 June 2023.

sources.title: Ministry of Finance Confirms Applicable Taxable Income Threshold for Corporate Tax Abu Dhabi, UAE

incentives.title: Free zone firms can pay 0%
incentives.text: A company in a free zone that meets the conditions of a Qualifying Free Zone Person pays 0% corporate tax on its qualifying income. Other income is taxed at 9%.

sources.title: Corporate Tax in the UAE

incentives.title: Dubai free zones waive fees
incentives.text: In April 2026 DIEZ froze rents on renewal and waived or deferred several licence fees in Dubai Silicon Oasis, Dubai Airport Freezone and Dubai CommerCity. It linked the relief to the regional situation. None of the measures targets data centres alone.

sources.title: Dubai Integrated Economic Zones Authority launches set of economic measures

data.title: Federal data protection law in force
data.text: Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021, the Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL), took effect on 2 January 2022. It requires consent for most processing and limits transfers of personal data abroad. It does not apply inside the DIFC and ADGM financial free zones, which have their own laws.

sources.title: Data protection laws in UAE - General - Data Protection Laws of the World
Data Protection & Privacy 2026 - UAE

data.title: PDPL detailed rules still not issued
data.text: The executive regulations that set out penalties and transfer details for the PDPL had not been issued as of March 2026. Firms get six months to comply once they are published.

sources.title: Data Protection & Privacy 2026 - UAE
Data protection laws in UAE - General - Data Protection Laws of the World

data.title: New federal AI and Data Authority
data.text: On 14 June 2026 the UAE created the Artificial Intelligence and Data Authority. It merges the UAE Data Office, the digital government arm of TDRA and the AI office, and reports to the Cabinet. It sets national data standards and proposes data laws.

sources.title: Mohammed bin Rashid approves establishing Artificial Intelligence and Data Authority
UAE unveils AI and data authority to create 'faster and smarter' government

data.title: Health data must stay in the UAE
data.text: Federal Law No. 2 of 2019 bars storing or processing health information outside the UAE. A health authority decision can allow exceptions.
data.authority: UAE Ministry of Health and Prevention

sources.title: Data Protection & Privacy 2026 - UAE

data.title: Cloud providers certified by Cyber Security Council
data.text: The UAE Cyber Security Council issued a National Cloud Security Policy on 6 February 2023. In May 2026 du's National Hypercloud became the first sovereign cloud certified under it. The certificate covers all government workloads except those classed Secret and Top Secret.

sources.title: The National Cloud Security Policy
du Tech's National Hypercloud Becomes the First Sovereign Cloud Certified by the UAE CSC

data.title: DIFC and ADGM run separate regimes
data.text: The DIFC applies its own Data Protection Law No. 5 of 2020. July 2025 amendments let people sue directly in DIFC courts. ADGM added rules in September 2025 on processing sensitive data without consent in some cases.
data.authority: DIFC Commissioner of Data Protection; ADGM Office of Data Protection

sources.title: Data Protection & Privacy 2026 - UAE

water.title: Abu Dhabi allows non-drinking water for cooling
water.text: The Abu Dhabi Department of Energy policy on water in district cooling plants lets operators use recycled water, desalinated water or seawater. The choice depends on cost and feasibility. District cooling used about 5% of the emirate's desalinated water when the policy launched.

sources.title: Abu Dhabi Department of Energy unveils the 'Water Management in District Cooling Plants' policy to promote district cooling system and decrease energy consumption

water.title: Abu Dhabi industrial water tariff
water.text: Industrial users in Abu Dhabi pay AED 7.84 per cubic metre for water. Recycled water costs AED 1.70 per cubic metre.

sources.title: Business Rates And Tariffs 2025

watching.title: G42 chip access lapses 6 April 2027
watching.text: The approval for G42 and Core42 to receive US chips without a licence expires on 6 April 2027 unless BIS says otherwise. If they have not become US companies by then, they must apply for authorisation.
watching.authority: US Bureau of Industry and Security

sources.title: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
sources.publisher: Federal Register (US Bureau of Industry and Security)

watching.title: G42 weighs majority US ownership
watching.text: Bloomberg reported on 4 September 2026 that G42 is exploring majority US ownership to keep its access to US AI chips. No deal had been announced by 3 October 2026.
watching.authority: US Bureau of Industry and Security

sources.title: Abu Dhabi's G42 Weighs US Ownership to Safeguard AI Chip Access

watching.title: Stargate UAE plan revised after strikes
watching.text: Reuters reported on 11 September 2026 that the UAE is revising the 5 GW Stargate UAE campus after Iranian strikes. Sources said it may become a network of hardened sites, some underground. The strikes hit AWS data centres in the UAE in March 2026.

sources.title: Exclusive-UAE Revises AI Data Center Plan After Iranian Attacks, Sources Say
AWS UAE suffers AZ outage after "objects strike data center" and cause fire, amid Iran attacks

watching.title: Abu Dhabi data centre tariff due
watching.text: Rates for the planned Abu Dhabi data centre tariff are still unpublished. Their level will set the cost gap with Dubai's roughly US$0.126 per kWh.

sources.title: Abu Dhabi to Introduce Dedicated Power Tariff for AI Data Centres

watching.title: PDPL rules may follow new authority
watching.text: The new AI and Data Authority took over the UAE Data Office in June 2026. Its creation could move the long-delayed PDPL executive regulations forward. No date has been set.
watching.authority: UAE Artificial Intelligence and Data Authority

sources.title: UAE unveils AI and data authority to create 'faster and smarter' government
Data Protection & Privacy 2026 - UAE
